1	# Godot — Breaking Changes
2	
3	Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.6 → 4.7 and the section dates); 2026-02-12 (older sections)
4	
5	Changes between Godot versions, focused on post-LLM-cutoff changes (4.4+).
6	
7	## 4.6 → 4.7 (Jun 2026 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)
8	
9	From the official migration guide
10	(https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html,
11	checked 2026-10-17). Rows marked **GDScript breaks** stop existing GDScript from
12	working; the rest add optional parameters, change C# compatibility only, or
13	change behaviour or defaults. The guide lists no deprecations.
14	
15	| Subsystem | Change | Details |
16	|-----------|--------|---------|
17	| GDScript | Overrides inherit a typed return | An override of a method with a typed return now inherits that type, so it needs an explicit `return` (add `return null` to fix the error). **GDScript breaks** |
18	| GDScript | Packed array element writes | Setting one element of a packed array no longer calls the setter of the whole packed-array property |
19	| GUI | `RichTextLabel.ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_IN_PERCENT` renamed | Now `UPDATE_WIDTH_UNIT`. **GDScript breaks** |
20	| GUI | `RichTextLabel.add_image()` / `update_image()` | `width` / `height` are `float` (were `int`); `width_in_percent` / `height_in_percent` renamed `width_unit` / `height_unit`, typed `RichTextLabel.ImageUnit` (were `bool`, default `false` → `0`). C# source breaks |
21	| GUI | `Control.accessibility_live` type | `AccessibilityServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` (was `DisplayServer.AccessibilityLiveMode`). C# breaks |
22	| Core | `Object.is_class()` | Parameter is `StringName` (was `String`) |
23	| Core | `OptimizedTranslation.generate()` | Returns `bool` (was `void`). C# binary breaks |
24	| Input | Mouse and keyboard device IDs | Were `0`; now `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` and `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`, because some joypads use `0`. Identify events by type or compare `InputEvent.device` to those constants |
25	| Physics | Jolt: `WorldBoundaryShape3D` plane sign | The sign of `plane.d` is read the way Godot Physics reads it, so it is flipped compared to 4.6: negate it to keep 4.6 behaviour |
26	| Physics | Jolt: `SoftBody3D` mass and stiffness | Mass defaults to 1 kg for the whole body (was 1 kg per point); `linear_stiffness` is applied differently. Re-tune `linear_stiffness` and `damping_coefficient` on every `SoftBody3D` |
27	| Physics | Jolt: `Area3D` and `SoftBody3D` | `Area3D` now reports overlaps with `SoftBody3D`; use collision layers and masks to ignore them |
28	| Physics | `PhysicsServer2D.body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision()` | Optional `direction` added; `PhysicsServer2DExtension._body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision()` requires it (extensions break) |
29	| Audio | `AudioStreamPlayer2D` / `AudioStreamPlayer3D` `area_mask` default | Changed from layer `1` to `0` (disabled). An `Area2D`/`Area3D` `audio_bus_override` that relied on the default mask stops working until the mask is set back to layer `1` |
30	| Audio | `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.tap_back_pos` | Removed. **GDScript breaks** where it is used |
31	| Rendering | `CanvasItem` line drawing | No antialiasing feather is added, so lines look thinner; widen lines that relied on the old thickness |
32	| Rendering | `LinearToSRGB` visual shader node | No longer clamps to `[0.0, 1.0]` under Forward+ and Mobile |
33	| Rendering | `get_format()` moved | From `ImageTexture` / `PortableCompressedTexture2D` to base class `Texture2D` |
34	| Rendering | `RenderingServer.particles_request_process_time()` | `time` renamed `process_time`; optional `process_time_residual` added (also on `request_particles_process()` of the four particle nodes) |
35	| Rendering | Sky reflection roughness layers | `rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers` default `7` → `8` |
36	| Animation | `Animation.length` | Type metadata `double` (was `float`). C# breaks |
37	| Animation | `LookAtModifier3D.relative` | Default `false` (was `true`) |
38	| Animation | `AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D/2D.add_blend_point()` | Optional `name` added |
39	| Project | Stretch defaults for NEW projects | `display/window/stretch/mode` `canvas_items` (was `disabled`), `display/window/stretch/aspect` `expand` (was `keep`). Existing projects keep their settings |
40	| Text | `ResourceImporterDynamicFont.hinting` | Default `3` (was `1`) |
41	| Editor | `EditorSceneFormatImporter` import constants | Moved into the `ImportFlags` enum (`IMPORT_SCENE`, `IMPORT_ANIMATION`, …). C# source breaks |
42	| Editor | `EditorVCSInterface._commit()` | New `amend` parameter; VCS plugins break |
43	| Editor | Asset Library replaced by the Asset Store | The editor workspace is now "Asset Store" (release notes: https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7/) |
44	| XR | `OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_register_metadata()` | New `interaction_profile_metadata` parameter; extensions break |
45	
46	## 4.5 → 4.6 (Jan 2026 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)
47	
48	| Subsystem | Change | Details |
49	|-----------|--------|---------|
50	| Physics | Jolt is now the DEFAULT 3D physics engine | New projects use Jolt automatically. Existing projects keep their setting. Some HingeJoint3D properties (like `damp`) only work with GodotPhysics. |
51	| Rendering | Glow processes BEFORE tonemapping | Was after tonemapping. Scenes with glow will look different. Adjust intensity/blend in WorldEnvironment. |
52	| Rendering | D3D12 default on Windows | Was Vulkan. For better driver compatibility. |
53	| Rendering | AgX tonemapper new controls | White point and contrast parameters added. |
54	| Core | Quaternion initializes to identity | Was zero. Unlikely to affect most code but technically breaking. |
55	| UI | Dual-focus system | Mouse/touch focus now separate from keyboard/gamepad focus. Visual feedback differs by input method. |
56	| Animation | IK system fully restored | CCDIK, FABRIK, Jacobian IK, Spline IK, TwoBoneIK via SkeletonModifier3D nodes. |
57	| Editor | New "Modern" theme default | Grayscale replaces blue-tint. Restore: Editor Settings → Interface → Theme → Style: Classic |
58	| Editor | "Select Mode" keybind changed | New "Select Mode" (v key) prevents accidental transforms. Old mode renamed "Transform Mode" (q key). |
59	| 2D | TileMapLayer scene tile rotation | Scene tiles can now be rotated like atlas tiles. |
60	| Localization | CSV plural form support | No longer requires Gettext for plurals. Context columns added. |
61	| C# | Automatic string extraction | Translation strings auto-extracted from C# code. |
62	| Plugins | New EditorDock class | Specialized container for plugin docks with layout control. |
63	
64	## 4.4 → 4.5 (Sep 2025 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)
65	
66	| Subsystem | Change | Details |
67	|-----------|--------|---------|
68	| GDScript | Variadic arguments added | Functions can accept `...` arbitrary params — new language feature |
69	| GDScript | `@abstract` decorator | Abstract classes and methods now enforceable |
70	| GDScript | Script backtracing | Detailed call stacks available even in Release builds |
71	| Rendering | Stencil buffer support | New capability for advanced visual effects |
72	| Rendering | SMAA 1x antialiasing | New post-processing AA option |
73	| Rendering | Shader Baker | Pre-compiles shaders — reportedly 20x faster startup on some demos |
74	| Rendering | Bent normal maps, specular occlusion | New material features |
75	| Accessibility | Screen reader support | Control nodes work with accessibility tools via AccessKit |
76	| Editor | Live translation preview | Test GUI layouts in different languages in-editor |
77	| Physics | 3D interpolation rearchitected | Moved from RenderingServer to SceneTree. API unchanged but internals differ. |
78	| Animation | BoneConstraint3D | New: AimModifier3D, CopyTransformModifier3D, ConvertTransformModifier3D |
79	| Resources | `duplicate_deep()` added | New explicit method for deep duplication of nested resources |
80	| Navigation | Dedicated 2D navigation server | No longer a proxy to 3D navigation; smaller export for 2D games |
81	| UI | FoldableContainer node | New accordion-style container for collapsible UI sections |
82	| UI | Recursive Control behavior | Disable mouse/focus interactions across entire node hierarchies |
83	| Platform | visionOS export support | New platform target |
84	| Platform | SDL3 gamepad driver | Delegated gamepad handling to SDL library |
85	| Platform | Android 16KB page support | Required for Google Play targeting Android 15+ |
86	
87	## 4.3 → 4.4 (Mar 2025 — BEFORE CUTOFF, VERIFY)
88	
89	| Subsystem | Change | Details |
90	|-----------|--------|---------|
91	| Core | `FileAccess.store_*` return `bool` | Was `void`. Methods: `store_8`, `store_16`, `store_32`, `store_64`, `store_buffer`, `store_csv_line`, `store_double`, `store_float`, `store_half`, `store_line`, `store_pascal_string`, `store_real`, `store_string`, `store_var` |
92	| Core | `OS.execute_with_pipe` | Added optional `blocking` parameter |
93	| Core | `RegEx.compile/create_from_string` | Added optional `show_error` parameter |
94	| Rendering | `RenderingDevice.draw_list_begin` | Many parameters removed; `breadcrumb` parameter added |
95	| Rendering | `Shader.set_default_texture_parameter()` / `get_default_texture_parameter()` | Parameter/return type changed from `Texture2D` to `Texture`; the shading language did not change |
96	| Particles | `.restart()` method | Added optional `keep_seed` parameter (CPU/GPU 2D/3D) |
97	| GUI | `RichTextLabel.push_meta` | Added optional `tooltip` parameter |
98	| GUI | `GraphEdit.connect_node` | Added optional `keep_alive` parameter |
99	
100	## 4.2 → 4.3 (In Training Data — LOW RISK)
101	
102	| Subsystem | Change | Details |
103	|-----------|--------|---------|
104	| Animation | `Skeleton3D.add_bone` returns `int32` | Was `void` |
105	| Animation | `bone_pose_updated` signal | Replaced by `skeleton_updated` |
106	| TileMap | `TileMapLayer` replaces `TileMap` | One node per layer instead of multi-layer single node |
107	| Navigation | `NavigationRegion2D` | Removed `avoidance_layers`, `constrain_avoidance` properties |
108	| Editor | `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX` | Renamed to `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX2GLTF` |
109	| Animation | AnimationMixer base class | AnimationPlayer and AnimationTree now extend AnimationMixer |

1	# Architecture Decision Registry
2	#
3	# PURPOSE: Single source of truth for key architectural stances that all ADRs
4	# must agree on. Skills check this before writing new ADRs to detect conflicts
5	# at authoring time — before stories are created against contradictory decisions.
6	#
7	# RULES:
8	#   - Register a stance when it constrains how OTHER systems must be built.
9	#     An internal implementation detail that affects only one ADR does not need
10	#     to be registered.
11	#   - Never delete entries — set status: "superseded_by: ADR-NNNN" instead,
12	#     quoted: unquoted, the second colon makes the file invalid YAML.
13	#   - When a stance changes: update the entry, set revised: to today's date,
14	#     add a comment with the old value, and run /architecture-review to check
15	#     what ADRs are now invalidated.
16	#   - adr: is the authoritative source. All other ADRs that depend on this
17	#     stance list themselves in referenced_by.
18	#
19	# WRITTEN BY: /architecture-decision (Phase 5 — after ADR is approved)
20	# READ BY:    /architecture-decision (Step 2 — before authoring begins)
21	#             /architecture-review (Phase 4 — cross-ADR conflict baseline)
22	#             /create-stories (to embed architectural constraints in stories)
23	#             /dev-story (to check implementation against accepted stances)
24	#
25	# SEARCH PATTERNS (for skills using Grep):
26	#   All state owners:       Grep pattern="^  - state:" path="docs/registry/architecture.yaml"
27	#   Who owns player_health: Grep pattern="state: player_health"
28	#   All signal contracts:   Grep pattern="pattern: signal"
29	#   Budget for combat:      Grep pattern="system: combat"
30	#   All forbidden patterns: Grep pattern="^  - pattern:" (forbidden_patterns section)
31	#   Superseded entries:     Grep pattern="superseded_by: ADR-"
32	#
33	# LAYOUT: the one shape .claude/scripts/registry.sh reads. Each section is a
34	#   key at column 0 holding a block list, or [] while it is empty. Each entry
35	#   starts with its section's name key ("- state:", "- contract:", "- system:"
36	#   or "- target_fps:" for the frame budget, "- purpose:", "- pattern:"), the
37	#   dash at column 2 (or 0, the same for every entry of a section); its fields
38	#   sit two columns past the dash. Quote a value that holds ": ", such as
39	#   "superseded_by: ADR-NNNN". A line in any other shape is reported as
40	#   unsupported layout, with its number.

# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## Architecture Decision Records (`docs/architecture/`)

Use the ADR template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`

**Required sections:** Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences,
ADR Dependencies, Engine Compatibility, GDD Requirements Addressed

**Status lifecycle:** `Proposed` → `Accepted` → `Superseded`
- Never skip `Accepted` — stories referencing a `Proposed` ADR are auto-blocked
- Use `/architecture-decision` to create ADRs through the guided flow

**TR Registry:** `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
- Stable requirement IDs (e.g. `TR-movement-001`) that link GDD requirements to stories
- Never renumber existing IDs — only append new ones
- Updated by `/architecture-review` Phase 8

**Control Manifest:** `docs/architecture/control-manifest.md`
- Flat programmer rules sheet: Required / Forbidden / Guardrails per layer
- Date-stamped `Manifest Version:` in header
- Stories embed this version; `/story-done` checks for staleness

**Validation:** Run `/architecture-review` after completing a set of ADRs.

## Engine Reference (`docs/engine-reference/`)

Version-pinned engine API snapshots. **Always check here before using any
engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## Architecture Decision Records (`docs/architecture/`)

Use the ADR template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`

**Required sections:** Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences,
ADR Dependencies, Engine Compatibility, GDD Requirements Addressed

**Status lifecycle:** `Proposed` → `Accepted` → `Superseded`
- Never skip `Accepted` — stories referencing a `Proposed` ADR are auto-blocked
- Use `/architecture-decision` to create ADRs through the guided flow

**TR Registry:** `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
- Stable requirement IDs (e.g. `TR-movement-001`) that link GDD requirements to stories
- Never renumber existing IDs — only append new ones
- Updated by `/architecture-review` Phase 8

**Control Manifest:** `docs/architecture/control-manifest.md`
- Flat programmer rules sheet: Required / Forbidden / Guardrails per layer
- Date-stamped `Manifest Version:` in header
- Stories embed this version; `/story-done` checks for staleness

**Validation:** Run `/architecture-review` after completing a set of ADRs.

## Engine Reference (`docs/engine-reference/`)

Version-pinned engine API snapshots. **Always check here before using any
engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

1	# Godot Rendering — Quick Reference
2	
3	Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.7 changes); 2026-02-12 (rest) | Engine: Godot 4.7
4	
5	## What Changed Since ~4.3 (LLM Cutoff)
6	
7	### 4.7 Changes
8	- **`AreaLight3D`**: real-time rectangular area lights
9	- **HDR output** on Windows, macOS, iOS, visionOS and Linux (Wayland)
10	- **`DrawableTexture2D`**: simple API for drawing on textures (4.7 release notes: https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7/)
11	- **`CanvasItem` lines**: no antialiasing feather, so lines look thinner
12	- **`LinearToSRGB` visual shader** no longer clamps to `[0.0, 1.0]` (Forward+, Mobile)
13	- **`get_format()`** moved from `ImageTexture` / `PortableCompressedTexture2D` to `Texture2D`
14	- **`rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers`** default `7` → `8` (4.7 migration guide: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html)
15	
16	### 4.6 Changes
17	- **D3D12 is the default rendering backend on Windows** (was Vulkan)
18	- **Glow processes before tonemapping** (was after) — uses screen blending mode
19	- **AgX tonemapper**: new white point and contrast controls
20	- **SSR overhauled**: better realism, visual stability, and performance
21	
22	### 4.5 Changes
23	- **Shader Baker**: Pre-compiles shaders to reduce startup time
24	- **SMAA 1x**: New anti-aliasing option (sharper than FXAA, cheaper than TAA)
25	- **Stencil buffer support**: Enables selective geometry masking/portal effects
26	- **Bent normal maps**: Directional occlusion encoded in normal map textures
27	- **Specular occlusion**: Ambient occlusion now correctly affects reflections
28	
29	### 4.4 Changes
30	- **`RenderingDevice.draw_list_begin`**: Many parameters removed; optional `breadcrumb` added
31	- **`Shader` default-texture methods**: `set_default_texture_parameter()` takes and
32	  `get_default_texture_parameter()` returns `Texture`, not `Texture2D` (the shading
33	  language's `sampler2D` / `texture()` did not change)
34	- **Particles `.restart()`**: Added optional `keep_seed` parameter
35	
36	### 4.3 Changes (in training data)
37	- **Compositor node**: `Compositor` + `CompositorEffect` for post-processing chains
38	
39	## Current API Patterns
40	
41	### Post-Processing (4.3+)
42	```gdscript
43	# Use Compositor node — NOT manual viewport shader chains
44	# Add Compositor as child of WorldEnvironment or Camera3D
45	# Create CompositorEffect resources for each post-process step
46	```
47	
48	### Anti-Aliasing Options (4.6)
49	```
50	Project Settings → Rendering → Anti Aliasing:
51	- MSAA 2D/3D: Hardware MSAA (quality but expensive)
52	- Screen Space AA: FXAA (fast, blurry) or SMAA (sharp, moderate cost)  # SMAA new in 4.5
53	- TAA: Temporal (best quality, ghosting on fast motion)
54	```
55	
56	### Rendering Backend Selection (4.6)
57	```
58	Project Settings → Rendering → Renderer:
59	- Forward+ (default): Full featured, desktop-focused
60	- Mobile: Optimized for mobile/low-end, limited features
61	- Compatibility: OpenGL 3.3 / WebGL 2, broadest hardware support
62	
63	Windows default backend: D3D12 (was Vulkan pre-4.6)
64	```
65	
66	## Common Mistakes
67	- Assuming Vulkan is the default backend on Windows (D3D12 since 4.6)
68	- Using manual viewport chains instead of Compositor for post-processing
69	- Passing or expecting `Texture2D` in `Shader.set_default_texture_parameter()` /
70	  `get_default_texture_parameter()` (the type is `Texture` since 4.4 — the shading
71	  language's `sampler2D` / `texture()` did not change)
72	- Not using Shader Baker for projects with many shader variants
73

1	# Godot — Breaking Changes
2	
3	Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.6 → 4.7 and the section dates); 2026-02-12 (older sections)
4	
5	Changes between Godot versions, focused on post-LLM-cutoff changes (4.4+).
6	
7	## 4.6 → 4.7 (Jun 2026 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)
8	
9	From the official migration guide
10	(https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html,
11	checked 2026-10-17). Rows marked **GDScript breaks** stop existing GDScript from
12	working; the rest add optional parameters, change C# compatibility only, or
13	change behaviour or defaults. The guide lists no deprecations.
14	
15	| Subsystem | Change | Details |
16	|-----------|--------|---------|
17	| GDScript | Overrides inherit a typed return | An override of a method with a typed return now inherits that type, so it needs an explicit `return` (add `return null` to fix the error). **GDScript breaks** |
18	| GDScript | Packed array element writes | Setting one element of a packed array no longer calls the setter of the whole packed-array property |
19	| GUI | `RichTextLabel.ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_IN_PERCENT` renamed | Now `UPDATE_WIDTH_UNIT`. **GDScript breaks** |
20	| GUI | `RichTextLabel.add_image()` / `update_image()` | `width` / `height` are `float` (were `int`); `width_in_percent` / `height_in_percent` renamed `width_unit` / `height_unit`, typed `RichTextLabel.ImageUnit` (were `bool`, default `false` → `0`). C# source breaks |
21	| GUI | `Control.accessibility_live` type | `AccessibilityServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` (was `DisplayServer.AccessibilityLiveMode`). C# breaks |
22	| Core | `Object.is_class()` | Parameter is `StringName` (was `String`) |
23	| Core | `OptimizedTranslation.generate()` | Returns `bool` (was `void`). C# binary breaks |
24	| Input | Mouse and keyboard device IDs | Were `0`; now `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` and `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`, because some joypads use `0`. Identify events by type or compare `InputEvent.device` to those constants |
25	| Physics | Jolt: `WorldBoundaryShape3D` plane sign | The sign of `plane.d` is read the way Godot Physics reads it, so it is flipped compared to 4.6: negate it to keep 4.6 behaviour |
26	| Physics | Jolt: `SoftBody3D` mass and stiffness | Mass defaults to 1 kg for the whole body (was 1 kg per point); `linear_stiffness` is applied differently. Re-tune `linear_stiffness` and `damping_coefficient` on every `SoftBody3D` |
27	| Physics | Jolt: `Area3D` and `SoftBody3D` | `Area3D` now reports overlaps with `SoftBody3D`; use collision layers and masks to ignore them |
28	| Physics | `PhysicsServer2D.body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision()` | Optional `direction` added; `PhysicsServer2DExtension._body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision()` requires it (extensions break) |
29	| Audio | `AudioStreamPlayer2D` / `AudioStreamPlayer3D` `area_mask` default | Changed from layer `1` to `0` (disabled). An `Area2D`/`Area3D` `audio_bus_override` that relied on the default mask stops working until the mask is set back to layer `1` |
30	| Audio | `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.tap_back_pos` | Removed. **GDScript breaks** where it is used |
31	| Rendering | `CanvasItem` line drawing | No antialiasing feather is added, so lines look thinner; widen lines that relied on the old thickness |
32	| Rendering | `LinearToSRGB` visual shader node | No longer clamps to `[0.0, 1.0]` under Forward+ and Mobile |
33	| Rendering | `get_format()` moved | From `ImageTexture` / `PortableCompressedTexture2D` to base class `Texture2D` |
34	| Rendering | `RenderingServer.particles_request_process_time()` | `time` renamed `process_time`; optional `process_time_residual` added (also on `request_particles_process()` of the four particle nodes) |
35	| Rendering | Sky reflection roughness layers | `rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers` default `7` → `8` |
36	| Animation | `Animation.length` | Type metadata `double` (was `float`). C# breaks |
37	| Animation | `LookAtModifier3D.relative` | Default `false` (was `true`) |
38	| Animation | `AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D/2D.add_blend_point()` | Optional `name` added |
39	| Project | Stretch defaults for NEW projects | `display/window/stretch/mode` `canvas_items` (was `disabled`), `display/window/stretch/aspect` `expand` (was `keep`). Existing projects keep their settings |
40	| Text | `ResourceImporterDynamicFont.hinting` | Default `3` (was `1`) |
41	| Editor | `EditorSceneFormatImporter` import constants | Moved into the `ImportFlags` enum (`IMPORT_SCENE`, `IMPORT_ANIMATION`, …). C# source breaks |
42	| Editor | `EditorVCSInterface._commit()` | New `amend` parameter; VCS plugins break |
43	| Editor | Asset Library replaced by the Asset Store | The editor workspace is now "Asset Store" (release notes: https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7/) |
44	| XR | `OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_register_metadata()` | New `interaction_profile_metadata` parameter; extensions break |
45	
46	## 4.5 → 4.6 (Jan 2026 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)
47	
48	| Subsystem | Change | Details |
49	|-----------|--------|---------|
50	| Physics | Jolt is now the DEFAULT 3D physics engine | New projects use Jolt automatically. Existing projects keep their setting. Some HingeJoint3D properties (like `damp`) only work with GodotPhysics. |
51	| Rendering | Glow processes BEFORE tonemapping | Was after tonemapping. Scenes with glow will look different. Adjust intensity/blend in WorldEnvironment. |
52	| Rendering | D3D12 default on Windows | Was Vulkan. For better driver compatibility. |
53	| Rendering | AgX tonemapper new controls | White point and contrast parameters added. |
54	| Core | Quaternion initializes to identity | Was zero. Unlikely to affect most code but technically breaking. |
55	| UI | Dual-focus system | Mouse/touch focus now separate from keyboard/gamepad focus. Visual feedback differs by input method. |
56	| Animation | IK system fully restored | CCDIK, FABRIK, Jacobian IK, Spline IK, TwoBoneIK via SkeletonModifier3D nodes. |
57	| Editor | New "Modern" theme default | Grayscale replaces blue-tint. Restore: Editor Settings → Interface → Theme → Style: Classic |
58	| Editor | "Select Mode" keybind changed | New "Select Mode" (v key) prevents accidental transforms. Old mode renamed "Transform Mode" (q key). |
59	| 2D | TileMapLayer scene tile rotation | Scene tiles can now be rotated like atlas tiles. |
60	| Localization | CSV plural form support | No longer requires Gettext for plurals. Context columns added. |
61	| C# | Automatic string extraction | Translation strings auto-extracted from C# code. |
62	| Plugins | New EditorDock class | Specialized container for plugin docks with layout control. |
63	
64	## 4.4 → 4.5 (Sep 2025 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)
65	
66	| Subsystem | Change | Details |
67	|-----------|--------|---------|
68	| GDScript | Variadic arguments added | Functions can accept `...` arbitrary params — new language feature |
69	| GDScript | `@abstract` decorator | Abstract classes and methods now enforceable |
70	| GDScript | Script backtracing | Detailed call stacks available even in Release builds |
71	| Rendering | Stencil buffer support | New capability for advanced visual effects |
72	| Rendering | SMAA 1x antialiasing | New post-processing AA option |
73	| Rendering | Shader Baker | Pre-compiles shaders — reportedly 20x faster startup on some demos |
74	| Rendering | Bent normal maps, specular occlusion | New material features |
75	| Accessibility | Screen reader support | Control nodes work with accessibility tools via AccessKit |
76	| Editor | Live translation preview | Test GUI layouts in different languages in-editor |
77	| Physics | 3D interpolation rearchitected | Moved from RenderingServer to SceneTree. API unchanged but internals differ. |
78	| Animation | BoneConstraint3D | New: AimModifier3D, CopyTransformModifier3D, ConvertTransformModifier3D |
79	| Resources | `duplicate_deep()` added | New explicit method for deep duplication of nested resources |
80	| Navigation | Dedicated 2D navigation server | No longer a proxy to 3D navigation; smaller export for 2D games |
81	| UI | FoldableContainer node | New accordion-style container for collapsible UI sections |
82	| UI | Recursive Control behavior | Disable mouse/focus interactions across entire node hierarchies |
83	| Platform | visionOS export support | New platform target |
84	| Platform | SDL3 gamepad driver | Delegated gamepad handling to SDL library |
85	| Platform | Android 16KB page support | Required for Google Play targeting Android 15+ |
86	
87	## 4.3 → 4.4 (Mar 2025 — BEFORE CUTOFF, VERIFY)
88	
89	| Subsystem | Change | Details |
90	|-----------|--------|---------|
91	| Core | `FileAccess.store_*` return `bool` | Was `void`. Methods: `store_8`, `store_16`, `store_32`, `store_64`, `store_buffer`, `store_csv_line`, `store_double`, `store_float`, `store_half`, `store_line`, `store_pascal_string`, `store_real`, `store_string`, `store_var` |
92	| Core | `OS.execute_with_pipe` | Added optional `blocking` parameter |
93	| Core | `RegEx.compile/create_from_string` | Added optional `show_error` parameter |
94	| Rendering | `RenderingDevice.draw_list_begin` | Many parameters removed; `breadcrumb` parameter added |
95	| Rendering | `Shader.set_default_texture_parameter()` / `get_default_texture_parameter()` | Parameter/return type changed from `Texture2D` to `Texture`; the shading language did not change |
96	| Particles | `.restart()` method | Added optional `keep_seed` parameter (CPU/GPU 2D/3D) |
97	| GUI | `RichTextLabel.push_meta` | Added optional `tooltip` parameter |
98	| GUI | `GraphEdit.connect_node` | Added optional `keep_alive` parameter |
99	
100	## 4.2 → 4.3 (In Training Data — LOW RISK)
101	
102	| Subsystem | Change | Details |
103	|-----------|--------|---------|
104	| Animation | `Skeleton3D.add_bone` returns `int32` | Was `void` |
105	| Animation | `bone_pose_updated` signal | Replaced by `skeleton_updated` |
106	| TileMap | `TileMapLayer` replaces `TileMap` | One node per layer instead of multi-layer single node |
107	| Navigation | `NavigationRegion2D` | Removed `avoidance_layers`, `constrain_avoidance` properties |
108	| Editor | `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX` | Renamed to `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX2GLTF` |
109	| Animation | AnimationMixer base class | AnimationPlayer and AnimationTree now extend AnimationMixer |
110

1	# Architecture Decision Registry
2	#
3	# PURPOSE: Single source of truth for key architectural stances that all ADRs
4	# must agree on. Skills check this before writing new ADRs to detect conflicts
5	# at authoring time — before stories are created against contradictory decisions.
6	#
7	# RULES:
8	#   - Register a stance when it constrains how OTHER systems must be built.
9	#     An internal implementation detail that affects only one ADR does not need
10	#     to be registered.
11	#   - Never delete entries — set status: "superseded_by: ADR-NNNN" instead,
12	#     quoted: unquoted, the second colon makes the file invalid YAML.
13	#   - When a stance changes: update the entry, set revised: to today's date,
14	#     add a comment with the old value, and run /architecture-review to check
15	#     what ADRs are now invalidated.
16	#   - adr: is the authoritative source. All other ADRs that depend on this
17	#     stance list themselves in referenced_by.
18	#
19	# WRITTEN BY: /architecture-decision (Phase 5 — after ADR is approved)
20	# READ BY:    /architecture-decision (Step 2 — before authoring begins)
21	#             /architecture-review (Phase 4 — cross-ADR conflict baseline)
22	#             /create-stories (to embed architectural constraints in stories)
23	#             /dev-story (to check implementation against accepted stances)
24	#
25	# SEARCH PATTERNS (for skills using Grep):
26	#   All state owners:       Grep pattern="^  - state:" path="docs/registry/architecture.yaml"
27	#   Who owns player_health: Grep pattern="state: player_health"
28	#   All signal contracts:   Grep pattern="pattern: signal"
29	#   Budget for combat:      Grep pattern="system: combat"
30	#   All forbidden patterns: Grep pattern="^  - pattern:" (forbidden_patterns section)
31	#   Superseded entries:     Grep pattern="superseded_by: ADR-"
32	#
33	# LAYOUT: the one shape .claude/scripts/registry.sh reads. Each section is a
34	#   key at column 0 holding a block list, or [] while it is empty. Each entry
35	#   starts with its section's name key ("- state:", "- contract:", "- system:"
36	#   or "- target_fps:" for the frame budget, "- purpose:", "- pattern:"), the
37	#   dash at column 2 (or 0, the same for every entry of a section); its fields
38	#   sit two columns past the dash. Quote a value that holds ": ", such as
39	#   "superseded_by: ADR-NNNN". A line in any other shape is reported as
40	#   unsupported layout, with its number.

381	# ─── FORBIDDEN PATTERNS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
382	# Architecture anti-patterns explicitly banned by accepted ADRs.
383	# When writing a new ADR, check this list — if the proposed approach matches
384	# a forbidden pattern, it must be reworked before the ADR can be Accepted.
385	#
386	# Register a pattern when an ADR explicitly bans it AND other ADRs might
387	# unknowingly use it (i.e., it's a tempting but wrong approach for this project).
388	
389	forbidden_patterns:
390	  - pattern: kernel_autoload_or_global
391	    status: active
392	    description: "No autoload, static variable or group lookup exposes the kernel, a block or a read view. The composition root injects the narrowest facet each module needs through setup()."
393	    why: "Hidden dependencies, shared state between headless tests, and no second kernel for MIRROR or replay comparison."
394	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0001-kernel-tick-driver-and-frame-order.md
395	    added: 2026-10-28
396	  - pattern: physics_callback_tick_source
397	    status: active
398	    description: "No kernel, simulation or presentation script defines _physics_process or _integrate_forces, and nothing is coupled to physics_jitter_fix or max_physics_steps_per_frame."
399	    why: "Two accumulators drift; the simulation has no physics body; the kernel GDD rejected it."
400	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0001-kernel-tick-driver-and-frame-order.md
401	    added: 2026-10-28
402	  - pattern: cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter
403	    status: active
404	    description: "Cosmetic animation phase uses present_time, never the tick counter; simulation-computed values use the committed tick."
405	    why: "Keeps pause, reduced motion and render rate from changing simulation-visible values."
406	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0001-kernel-tick-driver-and-frame-order.md
407	    added: 2026-10-28
408	  - pattern: await_process_frame_in_sim_or_presentation
409	    status: active
410	    description: "src/sim and src/presentation code does not await get_tree().process_frame; waiting is expressed in ticks or present_time."
411	    why: "That signal fires outside the per-node process_priority ordering (UNVERIFIED), outside the adapter-driver-presentation order."
412	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0001-kernel-tick-driver-and-frame-order.md
413	    added: 2026-10-28
414	  - pattern: command_constructed_outside_kernel
415	    status: active
416	    description: "Command.new() is called only inside src/kernel/ (_admit); issuer_peer, origin, seq and submission_id are never read from or written to payload data."
417	    why: "The stamped fields are the authority boundary; GDScript has no private constructors, so a run-time seal and a CI check enforce it."
418	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0002-authority-model-and-command-pipeline.md
419	    added: 2026-10-28
420	  - pattern: presentation_submit_without_handle
421	    status: active
422	    description: "Only the objects named at handle issue hold a SurfaceHandle or ControlHandle; subscribing as INPUT_SURFACE does not confer submit rights; SYSTEM commands are submitted only through ctx.submit_system inside a tick phase."
423	    why: "Presentation never writes the simulation (kernel H4); co-op must add ingress without changing owners."
424	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0002-authority-model-and-command-pipeline.md
425	    added: 2026-10-28
426	  - pattern: peer_id_keyed_persistent_state
427	    status: active
428	    description: "Persistent per-player state and ownership are keyed by PlayerId; the peer id appears only in the ingress stamp and binding table half (a). Ownership is never derived from scene-tree node authority."
429	    why: "Peer ids change on reconnect and host change; a copied save or re-join must keep its characters."
430	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0002-authority-model-and-command-pipeline.md
431	    added: 2026-10-28
432	  - pattern: write_outside_writescope_or_setter_dirty
433	    status: active
434	    description: "No block is written outside a kernel WriteScope (APPLY, PAUSED_APPLY, HOOK, INIT, RESTORE); every mutator begins with scope.open_for; dirty keys are marked only through scope.mark_dirty, never from a property setter."
435	    why: "Kernel CR-9 write discipline; 4.7 packed-array element writes no longer call setters, so setter-based dirty tracking silently misses changes."
436	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0003-state-block-registry-and-owner-contract.md
437	    added: 2026-10-28
438	  - pattern: void_or_value_returning_owner_callable
439	    status: active
440	    description: "No kernel-invoked owner callable is declared -> void or returns a domain value; each is -> CompletionToken with return ctx.complete() as its last statement; outcomes go through ctx."
441	    why: "An aborted GDScript function returns a default the caller cannot tell from a result; the completion sentinel is the only release-build abort guard."
442	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0003-state-block-registry-and-owner-contract.md
443	    added: 2026-10-28
444	  - pattern: block_as_resource_or_node
445	    status: active
446	    description: "State blocks are RefCounted plain data held by their owner, never a Resource or Node; restore copies into the existing block object."
447	    why: "Save-file trust (a .tres can embed scripts), canonical serialisation, scene-tree independence (H10), and long-lived read-view facades."
448	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0003-state-block-registry-and-owner-contract.md
449	    added: 2026-10-28
450	  - pattern: content_directory_scan
451	    status: active
452	    description: "Game code never enumerates res://assets/data with DirAccess; every data file is read by an explicit path from a committed, sorted manifest whose case matches the file on disk."
453	    why: "Listing order and names differ between editor and export; a stray file would load silently; Windows is case-insensitive, the package and the Deck are not."
454	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0007-static-content-data-pipeline-and-stable-type-ids.md
455	    added: 2026-10-28
456	  - pattern: mutable_or_resource_catalog
457	    status: active
458	    description: "No content catalog is a Resource, Node, autoload or static singleton, and none hands out a mutable container: arrays are read-only typed Array[T] stored once; packed arrays and per-call duplicate() are never returned."
459	    why: "Catalogs are shared by validate, P3 and presentation; packed arrays pass by reference and cannot be made read-only; duplicate() allocates (AC-69); many catalogs must coexist for tests and MIRROR."
460	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0007-static-content-data-pipeline-and-stable-type-ids.md
461	    added: 2026-10-28
462	  - pattern: position_derived_persisted_id
463	    status: active
464	    description: "No id that reaches a save, snapshot, hash or replicated record is an array index, file or manifest position, Dictionary order, path hash or ResourceUID; item type_id never reaches one; ledgers are append-only and retired ids are never reused."
465	    why: "Ids must keep their meaning across builds; a renumber would silently load the wrong def from an old save."
466	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0007-static-content-data-pipeline-and-stable-type-ids.md
467	    added: 2026-10-28
468	  - pattern: loader_side_effect_or_foreign_boot_code
469	    status: active
470	    description: "Content loaders return Array[BootError] with domain-2 codes from ContentFaults; they never call assert, push_error or quit, and never raise a content boot error from an owner system's own *_faults.gd."
471	    why: "assert is stripped in release, push_error trips gdUnit4, quit is untestable; one domain keeps src/data free of imports from Core and Feature fault files (ADR-0003 domain 2)."
472	    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0007-static-content-data-pipeline-and-stable-type-ids.md
473	    added: 2026-10-28

# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## Architecture Decision Records (`docs/architecture/`)

Use the ADR template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`

- Date-stamped `Manifest Version:` in header

Version-pinned engine API snapshots. **Always check here before using any
engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

703	## Architecture Principles
704	
705	1. **The simulation is the truth, and it is pure data.** Every gameplay fact lives in a kernel-registered state block owned by exactly one system, built from `RefCounted` objects and packed arrays, with no `Node`, no `Resource` and no scene-tree dependency. It runs headless and is unit-testable. *(Pillar 1; TD-FEASIBILITY risk "graph entangled with the scene tree".)*
706	2. **Every change is a command, and the host is the authority, even in single-player.** Player intent enters only as a plain-data command stamped with its issuer; cross-system writes go only through the owner's published mutators inside a kernel WriteScope. Co-op is a transport added later, not a rewrite. *(TD-FEASIBILITY B2.)*
707	3. **Presentation reads, never writes; perception never reaches the simulation.** Presentation subscribes to change notifications and draws from read views. A hallucination is a presentation-side transform through `perceived()`; `PERCEPTION_OUT` is unreadable from the simulation, and truth channels (trails, real light radius, character sprites, crewmate beams, physical consequences) never pass through the Filter. *(Pillar 4 guard rails; "no lie is unfalsifiable".)*
708	4. **Deterministic by construction.** Fixed 60 Hz integer ticks, integer state, ascending-id iteration, keyed RNG streams with persisted counters, and one hash definition. Same save bytes plus the same restore epoch and command stream give the same state hash. Determinism is what makes replay tests, save verification and later co-op mirroring possible.
709	5. **Versioned, verified persistence from v1.** Saves serialise data models, never scenes; every block carries a schema version migrated by its owner; every file is self-verifying and written atomically; a bad save never faults the kernel and never overwrites a good one. *(TD-FEASIBILITY: "save format not versioned from v1".)*
710	6. **Budgets are measured, not assumed.** Every performance claim is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; hot paths allocate nothing per tick; work is bounded by construction (caps and counted work units, never wall-clock), so a budget miss is a tuning change, not a redesign.

70	## System Layer Map
71	
72	### The layering rule
73	
74	The systems index orders systems by dependency (Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish). The architecture layers below are **responsibility** layers. One test decides the side: **a system that registers a SIM state block or a step hook is simulation; a system that registers none and only subscribes to the kernel is presentation.** Static content that is loaded once and never changes at runtime is data. The kernel and Save/Load are foundation because everything else registers with them.
75	
76	The simulation side never reads the presentation side. Presentation reads committed simulation state through read views and writes only engine-side nodes. The one presentation class that may change the simulation is `INPUT_SURFACE`, and it does so only by submitting commands.
77	
78	### Which way dependencies may point
79	
80	The stack is a responsibility stack, not a rule that dependencies only point down. The rules are:
81	
82	1. **Simulation to simulation, any direction.** Inside the simulation (Core and Feature), a module may call another module's read view or published mutator in either direction, as long as the step-hook graph the kernel topo-sorts stays acyclic. Examples that exist today: the Controller Sim (Core) reads Suit's `locomotion_cap` (Feature); Layout and the Graph call each other (`instantiate_section` one way, room identity the other). A consumer cannot finish before its provider exists or is stubbed, so these edges are sprint-ordering facts.
83	2. **No compile-time cycles.** Cross-system references go through `class_name` and typed interface base classes at the seams. `preload` of a sibling system's script is forbidden (a `preload` cycle fails to parse) and lint-checked (ADR-0010).
84	3. **Foundation host services read Feature state only through the kernel.** Save/Load polls owner read views (Assembly `last_shape_change_T`, Interaction `last_salvage_T`, the Attention view, Suit vitals) obtained through the kernel registry, never by importing those modules. The Pipeline root reads `body.state` the same way.
85	4. **Simulation never reads presentation.** One existing case breaks this: the Emitter reads the Failure & Trail glow table (`GLOW_BASE_PM`, `SEV_GLOW_PM`), which Failure & Trail owns. The table is static data, so it moves to Content data under ADR-0007; Failure & Trail still authors the values (IC-12). Presentation reads simulation only through read views and notifications.

148	### Engine awareness: Foundation and Core
149	
150	- **Kernel**: relies on `Node._process` ordering by `process_priority` and on `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` (LOW, but unverified for cross-node order, spike KRN-LAT-02); typed callables returning a `CompletionToken` (HIGH, 4.7 typed-return override rule); packed arrays with explicit dirty marking (HIGH, 4.7). *Reference: `breaking-changes.md` § 4.6 → 4.7, GDScript rows.*

559	**How an interface is expressed.** GDScript has no interfaces. ADR-0010 picks one mechanism for the seams: an `@abstract` base class (4.5+, HIGH, verify; fallback a plain base class whose methods `push_error`), or duck-typed contracts checked by a boot-time registry lint.

1	# ADR-0001: Kernel Tick Driver and Frame Order
2	
3	## Status
4	Proposed
5	
6	## Date
7	2026-10-28
8	
9	## Last Verified
10	2026-10-28 (against `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-1a, D.5 and `docs/engine-reference/godot/` 4.7). Engine behaviours marked UNVERIFIED below have not been run on 4.7.2.
11	
12	## Decision Makers
13	User (delegated all remaining design calls, 2026-10-28); Claude (author); reviewed by godot-specialist (engine: no blocking issues) and technical-director (TD-ADR: CONCERNS, amendments A1-A6, B7-B8 and C9-C13 applied in this revision).
14	
15	## Summary
16	The simulation kernel needs exactly one clock, and three approved design documents still describe two different ones (the kernel's `_process`-driven `TickDriver`, and an older physics-callback tick). This ADR fixes the kernel's source: one `TickDriver` driven from the `_process` of a single always-processing host node, with a fixed per-frame order set by named process-priority constants, `tick_alpha` as the only value presentation reads from the clock, and the kernel's services handed to each module as a narrow injected facet rather than through an autoload.
17	
18	## Engine Compatibility
19	
20	| Field | Value |
21	|-------|-------|
22	| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
23	| **Domain** | Core (frame loop, node processing order), with an Input boundary |
24	| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. Every API used predates the 4.3 cutoff, but the pinned engine reference is silent on cross-node `process_priority` order and on how `Engine.time_scale` scales `_process(delta)`, and 4.7 changed input device IDs. |
25	| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 → 4.7 GDScript and Input rows), `deprecated-apis.md`, `current-best-practices.md`, `modules/input.md`, `modules/physics.md` |
26	| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None. `Node._process`, `Node.process_priority`, `Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, `RefCounted`, `Engine.time_scale` and `roundi()` all exist in 4.3. |
27	| **Verification Required** | (1) Spike KRN-LAT-02: with the Input Adapter, the host node and a presentation node in one scene, the recorded `_process` call order is adapter → driver → presentation, on a dev build and on a release export. (2) `Engine.time_scale` scaling of `delta` (the kernel GDD marks it UNVERIFIED). (3) The first-frame `delta` after a long block (scene load, window drag, focus loss, a debugger breakpoint) is finite and handled by the cap and forgiveness, not a crash; the boundary service discards the first frame after a load (CR-1a). (3a) Delta jitter at `physics_jitter_fix` 0.5 versus 0, with `application/run/delta_smoothing` on and off, and the cost of the empty 60 Hz physics tick in an empty-scene baseline; the decision is to leave all three at engine defaults and record the measured effect on the 0-tick/2-tick frame pattern and on latency, not to claim they have nothing to do with the tick (MainTimerSync may adjust the idle step as well as the physics step, UNVERIFIED). (3b) `_input` and `_unhandled_input` are delivered before the frame's `_process` calls (UNVERIFIED in the reference), checked in the same scene as KRN-LAT-02. (4) `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` fires after every `_process` in the frame (owned by ADR-0008; recorded here because the camera write depends on this order). |
28	
29	## ADR Dependencies
30	
31	| Field | Value |
32	|-------|-------|
33	| **Depends On** | None (first ADR). The design source is `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-1, CR-1a and D.5. |
34	| **Enables** | ADR-0002 (command pipeline), ADR-0003 (block registry and hooks), ADR-0004 (notification and `tick_alpha` consumers), ADR-0006 (Save/Load boundary service timing), ADR-0008 (render pipeline: `present_time`, camera write), ADR-0009 (presentation subscriber contract), ADR-0019 (Input Adapter placement) |
35	| **Blocks** | Every epic that submits commands or draws from the clock: Player Controller, Pixel-Perfect Pipeline, Suit, Modular Ship Assembly (stories that quote the tick source), Interaction, Lighting. |
36	| **Ordering Note** | Do not **Accept** until the stale tick-source text is fixed in four GDDs and two architecture artifacts (see § GDD sync), spike KRN-LAT-02 has run (it now also checks `_input` delivery order and `time_scale`), and the TD-ADR amendments recorded below have been re-reviewed. If the spike fails, the sequential-parent fallback changes the Decision and the ADR needs a revision, not just a status change. Authoring now is safe because this ADR follows the kernel GDD (the owner), not the stale consumers. |
37	
38	## Context
39	
40	### Problem Statement
41	The game simulates at a fixed 60 Hz in integer ticks, and everything else (render, input, audio, camera) runs at the render rate. Something has to turn engine frames into whole ticks, say when input is read relative to those ticks, and say when presentation reads the result. The kernel GDD answers this in CR-1a: a `TickDriver` with an injected delta, driven from `_process`, with the physics step "never the clock". Three consumer GDDs (Player Controller, Suit, Pixel-Perfect Pipeline) and Modular Ship Assembly still describe the physics callback as the tick source, with `physics_jitter_fix` and `max_physics_steps_per_frame` couplings. Two accumulators drifting against each other is the failure that fixed-tick determinism cannot survive, so the choice has to be recorded once, in a place stories and the control manifest will cite.
42	
43	### Constraints
44	- **Determinism (kernel H9, CR-13).** The kernel never reads wall-clock time or `delta`. Ticks are whole, and the same save bytes plus the same command stream must produce the same state hash at any render rate.
45	- **Replay and test seams.** `Kernel.step()` is a plain synchronous method. Tests call it directly or inject `delta_us` into the driver; nothing in the kernel sleeps.
46	- **Main thread only (CR-1a).** The kernel, the driver and every owner callable run on the main thread.
47	- **No physics body on any simulation path (Ship Body BDY-3).** The avatar has none, so no sim code needs the physics callback.
48	- **Latency (D.4, KRN-LAT-01/02).** Submit-to-applied within one tick on an empty queue; `L_first` median ≤ 33.3 ms, p95 ≤ 50 ms on RM-DESKTOP.
49	- **Frame budgets (ruling R12).** P99 frame ≤ 16.6 ms on RM-DESKTOP (14.9 ms with headroom) and ≤ 33.3 ms on RM-DECK (30.0 ms), release export.
50	- **Coding standard.** Dependencies are injected, not reached through singletons, so headless tests can build their own kernel.
51	- **Engine reference silent** on cross-node `process_priority` order and on `Engine.time_scale` and `delta`.
52	
53	### Requirements
54	- One tick source, and the physics callback is not it.
55	- A fixed, lint-checkable order inside one rendered frame: input sample, then the tick loop, then presentation.
56	- A catch-up cap and a forgiveness rule so a slow frame degrades to slow motion, not a spiral.
57	- A single float handed to presentation that places a drawn pose between two committed ticks.
58	- No global `Kernel` name that sim or presentation code can reach without being given it.
59	
60	## Decision
61	
62	### 1. The tick source is `_process`, in one host node
63	
64	A single `KernelHost` node (`extends Node`, `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`) owns a `TickDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) and calls it from its own `_process(delta)`. The host does one thing with the engine's `delta`: it converts it once, `delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta * 1_000_000.0))`, and passes the integer to the driver. That conversion and the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads **that reach the simulation** (kernel H9). Presentation keeps its own `_process(delta)` for `present_time`, camera smoothing and cosmetic accumulators (Pipeline PR-9; Chart Table CT-43) and may read the committed tick `T` where the sim also computes the value (for example `beacon_aim(T)`, LO-27); none of that feeds back into the simulation. The driver is exactly the one specified in kernel CR-1a and D.5: an integer accumulator in units of microseconds × `TICK_RATE` (`TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 per tick), a boundary service before any tick, `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)`, a re-read of the kernel state after every `step()`, lag forgiveness (`LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0), result flush, and the paused service. This ADR does not restate those rules; the GDD is their authority. It records the *placement* and *order* decisions below.
65	
66	**The physics callback is not the clock and is not used by any simulation or presentation code in the MVP.** No script in `src/kernel/`, `src/sim/` or `src/presentation/` defines `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces`; `physics_interpolation` stays off. The kernel does not read `physics_jitter_fix`, `physics_ticks_per_second` or `max_physics_steps_per_frame`, and nothing is coupled to them, **but they can shape the `delta` the host receives** (the engine's main-loop timer sync produces both, UNVERIFIED), so the spike logs delta jitter at `physics_jitter_fix` 0.5 and at 0. Determinism does not depend on it, because replays inject `delta_us`. A boot check records `physics_ticks_per_second != TICK_RATE` in the diagnostics header as information, not as a failure. A later Vertical Slice physics projection (ADR-0033) runs in `_physics_process` as a read-only PROJECTOR and never steps the kernel.
67	
68	### 2. Frame order is fixed by named priority constants
69	
70	Godot runs `_process` in ascending `process_priority`, ties broken by tree order. Tree order is not a contract we want to depend on, so the order is fixed by three constants in one file, `src/kernel/process_priority.gd`:
71	
72	```gdscript
73	class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted
74	
75	## Lower values run first inside one rendered frame.
76	const INPUT_ADAPTER: int = -100   # INPUT_SURFACE objects only; samples input, calls submit()
77	const TICK_DRIVER: int = -50      # KernelHost: boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, result flush
78	const PRESENTATION: int = 0       # engine default; every presentation node, so a node that forgets to set it still runs after the driver
79	```
80	
81	The three-step order is therefore **input adapter → tick driver → presentation**, matching the kernel GDD's priority table (its ordinals 0, 1 and 2 are order only; the values above are the implementation). Choosing `PRESENTATION` as the engine default is deliberate: an unset node lands after the driver, which is the safe failure.
82	
83	Rules, each of which becomes a lint (ADR-0010):
84	- A node whose `process_priority` is below `TICK_DRIVER` must be a registered INPUT_SURFACE object. Nothing else may run before the driver. Scene files (`.tscn`) must not set `process_priority` at all (the Inspector stores a literal); code sets it from `ProcessPriority`. A regex cannot see priorities set at runtime, so the authoritative check is a **boot-time tree walk**: every node whose priority is below `TICK_DRIVER` is a registered INPUT_SURFACE object, only `KernelHost` uses `TICK_DRIVER`'s value, and every INPUT_SURFACE, `KernelHost` and presentation node resolves to the main-thread `process_thread_group`, because a sub-thread group leaves the main-thread ordering and breaks the main-thread rule. `process_thread_group` defaults to `INHERIT`, so the walk resolves each node's **effective** group by following `INHERIT` up through its ancestors to the first explicit value (the root counts as `MAIN_THREAD`); reading the node's own property alone would pass an `INHERIT` node under a `SUB_THREAD` parent. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review.)* Exactly which rules the lint tool can enforce statically and which move to boot walks is ADR-0010's call (OQ-16).
85	- No node other than `KernelHost` may use `TICK_DRIVER`'s value.
86	- A presentation node's `process_priority` is `PRESENTATION` or greater and is never set to a literal; it references the constant.
87	- Code in `src/sim/` and `src/presentation/` does not `await get_tree().process_frame` (that signal fires outside the per-node ordering, UNVERIFIED); waiting is expressed in ticks or in `present_time`.
88	
89	### 3. The Input Adapter samples and submits in its own `_process`
90	
91	The Adapter (an INPUT_SURFACE, Player Controller GDD PC-1(a)) reads device state and calls `submit()` from its `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`. It may latch raw events in `_input`/`_unhandled_input`, which the engine delivers before the frame's `_process` calls, but it submits only from `_process`. Its commands are therefore queued before the driver's boundary service and tick loop run, so an intent sampled in frame N sits in tick T's P1 batch, is applied in P2 and is integrated in P3 of the same tick: one tick of latency, never two. The Adapter never samples in `_physics_process`. Devices are identified by event type, not by `device == 0` (4.7 changed mouse and keyboard device IDs; ADR-0019).
92	
93	In a frame that runs several ticks (catch-up), the Adapter has submitted once, so only the first tick of that frame sees new commands. Continuing movement survives because intent state lives in `controller.state` and commands are edge- or change-based, not per-tick.
94	
95	### 4. `tick_alpha` is the only value presentation reads *from the driver*
96	
97	At the end of each driver frame the driver publishes `tick_alpha = clampf(float(acc) / float(TICK_UNITS), 0.0, 1.0)` (identical to kernel D.3's `t_since_last_commit / tick_duration`; the casts are required, because `acc` and `TICK_UNITS` are both `int` and an unmarked `/` is integer division in GDScript, which would give 0 on every normal frame and fail the `integer_division` warning policy). It is a presentation-only float: it is not a state block, is never hashed or saved, and the simulation never reads it (kernel H9). Presentation reads it once per frame in its own `_process` and interpolates previous-to-current committed state with `pos = floor(prev + (curr - prev) * tick_alpha)` (Pipeline Section D, interpolation formula; restore case in its Edge Cases). Because forgiveness at `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0 drops whole lag ticks at the end of every frame but keeps the sub-tick remainder, `acc < TICK_UNITS` after the driver runs in `RUNNING`, so `tick_alpha` is continuous and in [0, 1). **Two rules from kernel D.3 are binding and are restated here because they are easy to lose:** (1) **while the kernel is not `RUNNING` the driver holds `tick_alpha` at 1.0**, so a paused, loading or saving game draws the latest committed pose and never a frozen partway-back pose; (2) **on every transition into `RUNNING` the kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every `interpolated` block** (ADR-0003), so `previous == current` on resume and the first running frame, including a 0-tick frame, cannot interpolate across a discontinuity.
98	
99	Presentation also keeps a render-rate cosmetic clock, `present_time`, owned by the Pipeline root (Pipeline PR-9, ADR-0008). The rule recorded here: **cosmetic phase (flicker, gutter, fades) uses `present_time`; anything the simulation also computes (beacon aim, poses, wane) uses the kernel tick; the tick counter is never used for cosmetic phase** (Lighting LO-4).
100	
101	### 5. The kernel reaches modules by injection
102	
103	There is no `Kernel` autoload and no static singleton for kernel or game state. The main scene's root script (the **composition root**, `src/game/game.gd`) constructs the kernel, the `TickDriver` and the `KernelHost`, then gives every module and subscriber **the narrowest facet it needs through `setup()`**, never the whole `Kernel`: a simulation module receives the registration and mutator-scope services ADR-0003 defines; a presentation subscriber receives `subscribe(...)`, the read views and a read-only **`PresentationClock`** (`tick_alpha`, `T`, `running`, backed by the driver); and the right to submit or to call the control plane comes only from the named handles ADR-0002 defines, which the root issues to a few objects. Handing the whole kernel to presentation would give it `submit()`, which kernel CR-10 limits to INPUT_SURFACE. Headless tests construct their own kernel, driver and facets and need no scene. In the code examples in `docs/architecture/architecture.md`, `Kernel.` reads as "the injected facet". There are no recorded exceptions.
104	
105	### 6. Pause, load and the tree
106	
107	The kernel's `PAUSED` state is the only pause the simulation knows (kernel CR-16). `KernelHost` is `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, so the driver keeps running its boundary service whether or not anything pauses the scene tree, and no simulation code reads `SceneTree.paused`. Whether the UI layers use `SceneTree.paused` or per-layer `process_mode` is **not decided here**: the Chart Table GDD routes it to its own ADR candidate (a) and the Debug Overlay GDD (E-DO-48, AC-DO-174) assumes `SceneTree.paused` can be true; ADR-0030 decides it, and it must keep `KernelHost` and the Input Adapter `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`. Window focus loss, an OS-level stall, a debugger break or a long load simply produces one large `delta`: the cap (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` = 4) and forgiveness absorb it, and the accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`, so loads, saves and pauses never cause catch-up bursts afterwards (kernel CR-1a).
108	
109	### Architecture Diagram
110	
111	```
112	Engine main loop, one rendered frame (_process in ascending process_priority)
113	│
114	├─ -100  Input Adapter           [INPUT_SURFACE]   reads input → surface.submit(...)  (SurfaceHandle, ADR-0002)           (queued only)
115	│
116	├─  -50  KernelHost._process(delta)
117	│          delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta × 1e6))                  ← the only wall-clock read that reaches the sim
118	│          TickDriver.frame(delta_us):
119	│            1 boundary service (SAVING/LOADING/pause/resume; may clear acc, discard this frame's delta)
120	│            2 repeat ticks_run times, re-reading kernel state after each:
121	│                 Kernel.step() = P0 begin · P1 intake · P2 dispatch · P3 step hooks · P4 commit · P5 notify · P6 boundary
122	│            3 forgiveness (drop whole lag ticks, keep the sub-tick remainder)
123	│            4 flush the result buffer
124	│            5 if PAUSED: paused service
125	│          tick_alpha = clampf(float(acc) / float(TICK_UNITS), 0, 1)   (1.0 while not RUNNING)
126	│
127	└─   0   Presentation nodes      [PRESENTATION]    handlers already marked dirty at P5;
128	           (Pipeline root, Avatar Presenter, Lighting, Trail,        draw from committed views at tick_alpha;
129	            Instruments, HUD, Audio, Debug)                          Pipeline writes camera in frame_pre_draw
130	
131	_physics_process: not used by the kernel, simulation or presentation in the MVP.
132	```
133	
134	### Key Interfaces
135	
136	```gdscript
137	class_name TickDriver extends RefCounted
138	## Turns an injected wall-time delta into whole kernel ticks. No scene tree, no engine clock.
139	func _init(kernel: Kernel, params: TickParams) -> void
140	func frame(delta_us: int) -> TickFrameResult   # boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, flush; returns ticks_run, dropped, tick_alpha
141	var tick_alpha: float:                         # presentation-only; read once per frame
142		get: return _tick_alpha
143	
144	class_name KernelHost extends Node
145	func setup(driver: TickDriver) -> void         # called by the composition root; sets process_mode and process_priority
146	func _process(delta: float) -> void            # returns at once if setup() has not run (null driver); else delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta * 1_000_000.0)); driver.frame(delta_us)
147	
148	class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted  # constants shown in Decision § 2
149	
150	# Every module and subscriber:
151	func setup(facet: ModuleFacet) -> void         # the narrowest facet for the module's class (ADR-0003 / ADR-0009); stored; never looked up through a global
152	
153	class_name PresentationClock extends RefCounted  # read-only, backed by the TickDriver
154	var tick_alpha: float:
155		get: return _driver.tick_alpha                 # 1.0 while the kernel is not RUNNING
156	var T: int:
157		get: return _kernel_clock_t()                  # last committed tick
158	var running: bool:
159		get: return _kernel_running()
160	```
161	
162	### Implementation Guidelines
163	- **Must** drive `Kernel.step()` only from `TickDriver.frame()`, and call `TickDriver.frame()` only from `KernelHost._process`. Tests may call either directly.
164	- **Must never** define `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces` in `src/kernel/`, `src/sim/` or `src/presentation/`.
165	- **Must** use the `ProcessPriority` constants; **must never** write a literal `process_priority` value.
166	- **Must** submit input only from the Input Adapter's `_process`; **must never** call `submit()` from `_input`, `_physics_process` or a signal handler.
167	- **Must** pass each module its facet with `setup()`; **must never** add an autoload, a static variable or a group lookup that exposes the kernel, a block or a read view, and **must never** give a presentation node the whole `Kernel`.
168	- **Must** read `tick_alpha` through `PresentationClock` in presentation only, never in a simulation callable, and **must never** use the tick counter for cosmetic animation phase.
169	- **Must** keep `Engine.time_scale = 1.0` in release builds; a boot check records `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT` in diagnostics otherwise. A boot assertion also requires `application/run/low_processor_mode` to be false (in low-processor mode the engine idles between events, the simulation would stall and the next `delta` would spike), and the diagnostics header records `Engine.max_fps`, the vsync mode and `physics_ticks_per_second`.
170	- **Must** keep the `delta_us` conversion in `KernelHost` and nowhere else; the lint for forbidden clock APIs (`Time.get_ticks_msec`, `Time.get_ticks_usec`, `Time.get_unix_time_from_system`, `Time.get_datetime_dict_from_system`, `Time.get_time_dict_from_system`, `get_process_delta_time`, `Engine.get_frames_drawn`, `Engine.get_process_frames`) allow-lists only `KernelHost` and the diagnostics timer. (`OS.get_ticks_*` and `OS.get_unix_time*` do not exist in Godot 4, so linting them catches nothing; see `deprecated-apis.md`.) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review.)*
171	- **Should** test the driver with injected `delta_us` sequences (16,000 / 16,667 / 17,334 µs patterns, 100 ms hitches, zero-length frames) and the frame order with a recording scene (KRN-LAT-01, KRN-LAT-02).
