56	*Specialists consulted: systems-designer (primary), engine-programmer, gameplay-programmer, game-designer, ux-designer. Disagreements resolved and logged 2026-10-26; items the specialists could not resolve are in Open Questions.*
57	
58	
59	**Vocabulary.** *Base px* (*art px*): one pixel of the 640×360 logical grid. *Screen px*: one pixel of the window. *k*: the world's integer scale (screen px per base px). *k_base*: the effective base scale — the manual `k` when Settings sets one below Auto, else the automatic `k` (C6, D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *H*: the HUD's integer scale, independent of k. *Picture*: the region of the window that shows the game (the window unless letterboxed). *World viewport*: the `SubViewport` holding every lit thing; its canvas **is the current body's frame** (PR-6 C2). *Body*: a Ship Body & Interior Physics object with its own reference frame (home-ship, derelict, pod, detached section). *Sort origin*: the base-px row an object sorts by on the Y-sorted layer. *Pose*: the camera's output — integer base-px position in the body frame plus the current k. *`present_time`*: the pipeline's render-rate clock (PR-9). *Tick*, *`tick_alpha`*, *read view*, *`PRESENTATION`*: as the kernel GDD defines them (CR-10, CR-11, D.3).
60	
61	---
62	
63	**PR-1. Logical resolution and integer scale.** The world is authored at **640×360 base px** (registry: `BASE_RESOLUTION`) (art bible 8.1, decided) and drawn at an integer scale `k = floor(min(W / 640, H / 360))` where `W × H` is the window's **pixel** size — never derived from DPI; `content_scale_factor` stays 1.0 and `allow_hidpi` behaviour on the Deck and on Windows ≥ 125 % scaling is logged by spike step 11 (→ D for the variable table). The **minimum window is 1280×720** (registry: `MIN_WINDOW`) (C-R; `Window.min_size` `[BIN]`), so `k ≥ 2` on every display. Nothing in the world is ever drawn at a non-integer scale; the only non-integer text anywhere is the vector reading face on the chart-table layer (7.1). At every window size the player sees square, unblurred base pixels; the trade is the picture size, never pixel integrity. The player may choose k below the automatic value in Settings ("integer world scale: Auto + list", PR-14) — see PR-2 for why a manual k forces `keep`.
64	
65	| Window (screen px) | k | `keep`: picture and bars | `expand`: logical size (base px) | Tiles in view (expand) |
66	|---|---|---|---|---|
67	| 1280×720 | 2 | 1280×720, none | 640×360 | 13.3 × 7.5 |
68	| **1280×800 (Steam Deck)** | 2 | 1280×720, 40 top + 40 bottom | 640×400 | 13.3 × 8.3 |
69	| 1366×768 | 2 | 1280×720, 43/43 L/R, 24/24 T/B | 682×384 (even; 1/1 residual) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | 14.2 × 8.0 |
70	| 1365×768 (odd width) | 2 | 1280×720, 42/43 L/R, 24/24 T/B | 682×384 (the logical size is always even, so the engine never sees an odd or fractional base; the 1 px residual is letterboxed, 0/1 — what the engine draws in it is step 11's) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | 14.2 × 8.0 |
71	| 1600×900 | 2 | 1280×720, 160/160 L/R, 90/90 T/B (36 % of the screen black) | 800×450 | 16.7 × 9.4 |
72	| **1920×1080** | 3 | none | 640×360 | 13.3 × 7.5 |
73	| 1920×1200 | 3 | 1920×1080, 60/60 T/B | 640×400 | 13.3 × 8.3 |
74	| **2560×1440** | 4 | none | 640×360 | 13.3 × 7.5 |
75	| 2560×1080 (21:9) | 3 | 1920×1080, 320/320 L/R | 852×360 (even; 2/2 residual) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | 17.8 × 7.5 |
76	| **3440×1440 (ultrawide)** | 4 | 2560×1440, 440/440 L/R | 860×360 | 17.9 × 7.5 |
77	| **3840×2160** | 6 | none | 640×360 | 13.3 × 7.5 |
78	
79	*Rationale.* 640×360 is the only common base that lands on an integer at 720p, 1080p, 1440p and 2160p (8.1's table), so the four sizes the bible calls common need no policy at all; PR-2 exists for everything else. *Alternative rejected:* fractional scaling with a sharpening filter — it breaks 8.0's single grid and makes the 1 px contour, the 2 px bands and the 2 px fringe uneven widths, which 5.6's minimum-feature rule forbids. *Engine fact that makes this rule load-bearing:* `project.godot` today has no `[display]` block and no `rendering/textures` or `rendering/2d/snap` keys, so the project currently runs at the engine built-ins — 1152×648, stretch `disabled`, `fractional`, LINEAR-filtered, unsnapped `[BIN]` — and looks "almost right" in the editor at 1×. PR-15 is the guard.
80	
81	---
82	
83	**PR-2. Aspect: `keep` for the spike, `expand` as the IDEAL, both bounded; bars are true black.**
84	
85	- **`keep` (letterbox).** The picture is `640k × 360k`, centred; the remainder is bars. This is the spike architecture (8.4) and the **default until 8.12 step 2 and step 11 have run**, because the world viewport is a fixed 640×360 and nothing resizes.
86	- **`expand` (IDEAL, 8.1/8.10, post-spike).** The world viewport's logical size becomes `(2·floor(W/(2k)), 2·floor(H/(2k)))` (always even; D.3), clamped to **≤ 960×540** at default zoom (PROVISIONAL cap = 1.5× base; → D), remainder letterboxed; the base size and k both stay integer at every window (C-R); the **HUD rect is pinned to the `k_base` picture rect** (never the window, never the zoomed picture), so the HUD does not move on a zoom step even when a ladder field leaves a few black pixels inside it (D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The camera stays centred on the same target, so an ultrawide player sees more void left and right and a Deck player 20 more rows above and below.
87	- **Manual k forces `keep`.** A player-chosen k below the automatic value under `expand` would be a permanently wider frame (at 1080p, k = 2 gives 960×540 — exactly the zoom-out view, as the default), which the game-designer's decision forbids ("never a wider default frame"; the frame is changed only by the player's `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` steps, PR-6 C6 *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check)*). So when `k < k_auto`, aspect is `keep` regardless of the setting. *(Systems-designer resolution of a conflict between the Settings list and the camera decision — flagged for the ux-designer and game-designer to confirm.)*
88	
89	*The honesty caveat on "more void, not more information" (8.1).* The claim holds in the dark states (2.4–2.8), where everything outside the beam is black whichever width the frame is. It does **not** fully hold in two cases: (i) at 3440×1440 under `expand` the half-width is ≈ 9 tiles, so the narrow cone's 8-tile reach (8.3) fits entirely on screen where a 16:9 player's is clipped at 6.7 tiles; (ii) in the home-ship stable state (2.3) every fixture is on and a wider frame shows more lit ship. A 1600×900 player under `expand` sees 25 % more in each axis than a 1080p player. The cap bounds the gap; it does not remove it. **Routed to creative-director** with the recommendation to accept `expand` (a third of the screen black at 1600×900 is a worse experience than a slightly wider frame in a co-op horror game with no competitive stake) and to record the gap in Edge Cases. Second cost: under pass B (PR-7) light is paid per lit screen pixel — 4.95 M px at 3440×1440 against 2.07 M at 1080p; under pass A the cost grows only to 860×360 base px. The spike measures pass B at 1080p only; `expand` under pass B is a post-spike measurement.
90	
91	*Bars.* Letterbox bars are **true black, outside the world `SubViewport`**, untouched by the Perception Filter pass and by any camera jolt (C-R). Because the void inside the world is also near-black (0–1 % ambient, 2.5), a bar could be mistaken for unlit hull: the ux-designer recommends a **1-HUD-px Graphite hairline at the picture edge** — routed to art-director (it is a UI mark, 4.6 palette). What the engine actually draws in the remainder under `keep` is NOT SOURCEABLE (step 11).
92	
93	*Deck safe area (PROVISIONAL).* The HUD is authored **anchor-relative to the visible picture rect**, never the window, with the 7.0 safe margin of 5 % of the picture rounded up to whole HUD px per axis (registry `safe_margin`, the HUD & Suit Layer's formula): 32 × 18 HUD px at 1920×1080, H 3; 22 × 14 HUD px at 1280×800, H 3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)* — and must survive a fractional HUD canvas (the picture divided by H is not always integer) and both aspects (C-R). The Deck has no notch; the margin is ergonomic and the ux-designer may raise it per device. Deck *text* size is PR-12's problem.
94	
95	*Fullscreen.* Default `MODE_FULLSCREEN` (borderless window covering the screen, `Window.mode = 3` `[BIN]`) rather than `EXCLUSIVE_FULLSCREEN` for Alt-Tab safety `[UNV]`; any mode or size change fires `Viewport.size_changed` `[BIN]` and is handled as one `RESCALING` frame (C.2) by **one pipeline-root node that is the only writer** of `SubViewport.size`, `size_2d_override` and the camera limits rect (consumed by the solver, C8), and the only caller of `HudLayout` (the HUD & Suit Layer's layout function, which computes the HUD anchors) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)* (→ ADR, with PR-7's wiring).
96	
97	---
98	
99	**PR-3. The layer model.** One root viewport, one world viewport, and `CanvasLayer`s above it. The question that assigns a thing to a layer is 7.0's: *who produced the information?* — the ship goes in the world and must be lit to read; the suit and the chart table are screen-space and never lit. **The HUD is in a different viewport, not merely a different layer** (engine-programmer): world lights, glow, `CanvasModulate`, the Filter pass on the container and the camera transform cannot reach it by construction, so HR-1, HR-6 and HR-13 are promised structurally. The trade-off is that nothing that must *mix* (a diegetic element lit by the world) may live there — it goes in the world.
100	
101	| # | Layer (bottom → top) | Where | Scaled by | Lit / glow / ambient / occlusion | Perception Filter | Camera jolt | Contents |
102	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
103	| 0 | **World** | `SubViewport` inside a `SubViewportContainer` | k | **yes** — the only layer that is (`use_hdr_2d`, `use_debanding`, filter, snap set on this viewport's own members `[BIN]`; never on the root, which stays SDR-exact for the 4.6 palette) | per-node effects inside; the full-screen pass sits on the container (PR-10) | yes (bounded, PR-6 C7) | floors, floor marks, the Y-sorted layer, caps, lights, occluders, fringe, dust, horrors, web, in-world instruments, the camera |
104	| 1 | **Transit / load hold** | `CanvasLayer` | — | no | no | no | one opaque black quad, shown only in `TRANSIT_HOLD` and `BOOTING/LOADING` (C.2) |
105	| 2 | **Suit layer (HUD)** | `CanvasLayer` | H | **no** (HR-1 by construction) | no — readings are fed *perceived values* by the Filter as data; the frame is fed nothing (7.6 hand-off) | **never** (HR-13); prompts use the unjolted transform (C11) | critical strip, suit panel, hand rail, crew strip, interaction prompts, inspect card |
106	| 3 | **Chart table / menus** | `CanvasLayer` | H (bitmap face), continuous (reading face) | no | no | no | pause panel over the frozen world (7.4), web map, settings, text chat |
107	| 4 | **Debug overlay** | `CanvasLayer`, dev builds only | H | no | **no — it reads the true channel** | no | DIAGNOSTIC surface (C.3); may toggle debug draws *inside* the world viewport (note e) |
108	
109	Rules that follow: (a) **glow is per viewport** (8.11 flag 3; 4.6 reworked glow to run before tonemapping `[REF]`, so no older tuning transfers and `glow_hdr_threshold` is re-found at 8.12 step 8). (b) The ambient-floor hull material (8.11 flag 1) and the HR-15 low-vision raise are **Lighting's**, applied inside layer 0; the pipeline owns no ambient value and **no full-frame gamma or brightness control exists anywhere** (C-R): the only brightness control the game has is HR-15's bounded hull-material step, which can never reveal web, horrors or filaments and never touches the HUD. (c) In-world instruments are layer-0 lit sprites; the inspect card (7.0) is layer 2 — the same reading drawn twice, once lit and once not. (d) Interaction prompts are layer 2 and are *gated* by the Emitter State exposure query, never by the renderer. (e) Debug draws inside the world (occluder outlines, sort origins, the look-ahead box, the pixel grid, the camera limits) are children of a debug node in layer 0 that exists only in dev builds; `draw_line` there needs explicit width ≥ 1 base px because 4.7 lines have no feather `[REF]`. (f) **NEAREST is set in three places with two differently numbered enums `[BIN]`:** the project setting `rendering/textures/canvas_textures/default_texture_filter = 0` and the world `SubViewport.canvas_item_default_texture_filter = 0` use `Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST = 0`; the `SubViewportContainer.texture_filter` (a `CanvasItem` member, default `0 = PARENT_NODE`) must be set to `CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST = 1`, or pass A's ×k upscale is bilinear-blurred `[UNV]`. Whether project settings propagate into a `SubViewport` is NOT SOURCEABLE; the startup assertion (PR-15) reads every member back. (g) `SubViewport.size` defaults to 512×512 and `TileSet.tile_size` to 16×16 `[BIN]` — both are set explicitly (640×360 / 48×48); a scene that forgets gets silently wrong output.
110	
111	*Alternative rejected:* HUD inside the world viewport with `LIGHT_MODE_UNSHADED` materials — unshaded items still receive glow and the full-screen Filter pass, so HR-1 would be a per-node discipline that one forgotten material breaks (8.11 flag 3 made this call; recorded here because the pipeline inherits it).
112	
113	---
114	
115	**PR-4. Pixel integrity.** Inside the world viewport:
116	
117	1. **Nearest sampling everywhere** (`light_` textures excepted — sampled by the light, not the item, 8.4). Mipmaps off on every drawn sheet (8.7).
118	2. **Integer base-px placement by presentation code — the viewport snap flags are a safety net, not the mechanism** (gameplay-programmer, engine-programmer). Every presentation node computes `pos = floor(prev + (curr − prev) × tick_alpha)` in base px **in the current body frame** and writes that integer; `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` are on as belt-and-braces (what they snap to under pass B — base px or render px — is NOT SOURCEABLE; step 12 checks for double-rounding flicker at .5 boundaries). `floor` is the one rounding function used everywhere, including the camera and the beam's chest point (which uses the same rounded position as the sprite, so light origin and sprite never disagree). Because the world canvas *is* the body frame (PR-6 C2), no fractional body offset ever enters an interior position; other bodies drawn in this frame (a docked derelict, a detaching section) are placed by one floored offset shared by all their items, so their items never swim against each other.
119	3. **Interpolate, then quantise.** Rounding before interpolating produces 1 px stalls; interpolating after rounding is impossible. Consequence to state honestly (engine-programmer): **snap is a floor, not a filter** — interpolation changes only the *timing* of one-base-px steps, never their size. A body moving 1 base px per tick shows a k×k screen block step whenever it moves; the promise is "base-pixel steps at interpolated timing, never twice in a frame at f_render ≥ 60 (below that 1–2 base px per frame at 30–59 fps), never backward", not sub-pixel smoothness *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4)*. The Player Controller should therefore choose walk and run speeds in **whole base px per tick** when the camera quantum is 1 (PR-6 C3) — routed.
120	4. **Scale.** Only integer scales, only k (or the zoom step). Horizontal flips are permitted (mirrored facings, 5.6). No per-node scale animation of any kind; `Control.scale` stays `(1,1)` on the HUD. `Camera2D.zoom` stays `(1,1)` **always** (there is no pixel-snap member on `Camera2D` — confirmed by the exhaustive `[BIN]` member list — so zoom is a change of k, PR-6 C6).
121	5. **Rotation.** `Camera2D.rotation = 0` always, forever (game-designer; also `ignore_rotation = true` default `[BIN]`). Human-built geometry — floors, walls, caps, doors, props, machinery, pipes, seams, characters, tools, overlays, HUD — is **never rotated at runtime** (8.4): a lint asserts `rotation == 0` on every node under the environment, pipe, prop and actor groups. Rotation is permitted for **web pieces** (off-grid by design, 3.3), **horror rig segments** (quantised to 15°, stepped at 12 fps = every 5th tick, 5.4/8.10 — a test), and **lights** (engine light lives off the grid by 8.0's rule). Horror Entities' floor marks (smear, rime, radial hairlines, struck) are **not** web pieces: they are flip-only and never rotated (Horror C-HE-1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from horror-entities)*. What "rotated segments fall off the grid" means per pass: under pass A a rotated segment is rasterised at base resolution — a stair-step of whole base px, on the grid; under pass B it is rasterised at window resolution with nearest sampling — angled k×k blocks, same density, **off** the grid. The second is tolerated for horrors and web only (8.4); if it fails review the remedies are 8.10's (24-angle pre-rotated sets, or a base-resolution sub-viewport for horrors alone → ADR). `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel`'s effect on a rotated quad's corners is NOT SOURCEABLE — step 2 judges the rotating segment. Sub-pixel blur is forbidden in every case.
122	6. **Half-pixel origins.** `Sprite2D.centered = true` by default `[BIN]`: an odd-dimension texture centred puts its origin on a .5 and wobbles 1 px under NEAREST. 8.2's cells are even (48, 80, 96) and the foot origin (horizontally centred, the top row of the `foot_box`; registry `foot_box`) is set via `offset` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics)*, so the asset standard satisfies this; the rule for VFX and one-off sprites is **even cells, or `centered = false` with an integer `offset`**.
123	7. **No sub-pixel sprite positions** means no item is ever drawn at a fractional base-px offset *relative to the grid the other items are on*. Whether the whole grid may translate by screen pixels is the camera quantum's question (PR-6 C3), not this rule's.
124	8. **One interpolator.** The kernel's `tick_alpha` with previous/current read views is the only interpolator of sim-owned motion: `physics/common/physics_interpolation = false`, every presentation node `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF`, `Camera2D.position_smoothing_enabled = false`, `limit_smoothed = false` `[BIN]`. Decisive `[BIN]` reason beyond "two clocks": `get_global_transform_interpolated()` exists on `Node3D` only, so no 2D script could read where an engine-interpolated body is actually drawn — the camera would follow the un-interpolated pose and swim 1–3 render px against the sprite at 144 fps while looking fine at 60. The 2D interpolation machinery does exist in 4.7.2 `[BIN]` (items, lights, occluders); its behaviour is NOT SOURCEABLE and it is simply not used for sim-owned transforms. → ADR (interpolation clock). Whether pure-physics debris may use it is Ship Body's.
125	9. **Light masks.** `Light2D.range_item_cull_mask` and `CanvasItem.light_mask` default to bit 1 `[BIN]`; the unshaded emissive overlay and the fringe sprites go on a light-mask bit the beams do not light (6.2 "unshaded") — behaviour `[UNV]`, checked at 8.12 step 4. The HUD needs none; it is in another viewport. Bit 3 (decoys) and bits 4 and up (one per live body) are allocated by Lighting (LO-24) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from 2d-lighting-and-occlusion)*.
126	10. **Lines are sprites.** Hairlines, filaments and seams are sprites, never runtime line draws (8.4, `[REF]`).
127	
128	---
129	
130	**PR-5. Projection convention and the draw-order contract (3/4 oblique).** The projection is 1:1 with no foreshortening (8.2): one base px of floor depth, one of width and one of height are each one screen row or column. Floors are 48×48 squares (registry: `TILE_PX`). A wall has a **24 px footprint** on the floor grid, a **72 px front face** and a **24 px top cap**, occupying 96 screen rows but half a tile of floor.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

59	**Vocabulary.** *Base px* (*art px*): one pixel of the 640×360 logical grid. *Screen px*: one pixel of the window. *k*: the world's integer scale (screen px per base px). *k_base*: the effective base scale — the manual `k` when Settings sets one below Auto, else the automatic `k` (C6, D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *H*: the HUD's integer scale, independent of k. *Picture*: the region of the window that shows the game (the window unless letterboxed). *World viewport*: the `SubViewport` holding every lit thing; its canvas **is the current body's frame** (PR-6 C2). *Body*: a Ship Body & Interior Physics object with its own reference frame (home-ship, derelict, pod, detached section). *Sort origin*: the base-px row an object sorts by on the Y-sorted layer. *Pose*: the camera's output — integer base-px position in the body frame plus the current k. *`present_time`*: the pipeline's render-rate clock (PR-9). *Tick*, *`tick_alpha`*, *read view*, *`PRESENTATION`*: as the kernel GDD defines them (CR-10, CR-11, D.3).

The **minimum window is 1280×720** (registry: `MIN_WINDOW`) (C-R; `Window.min_size` `[BIN]`), so `k ≥ 2` on every display. Nothing in the world is ever drawn at a non-integer scale; the only non-integer text anywhere is the vector reading face on the chart-table layer (7.1). At every window size the player sees square, unblurred base pixels; the trade is the picture size, never pixel integrity. The player may choose k below the automatic value in Settings ("integer world scale: Auto + list", PR-14) — see PR-2 for why a manual k forces `keep`.

90	
91	*Bars.* Letterbox bars are **true black, outside the world `SubViewport`**, untouched by the Perception Filter pass and by any camera jolt (C-R). What the engine actually draws in the remainder under `keep` is NOT SOURCEABLE (step 11).
92	
93	*Deck safe area (PROVISIONAL).* The HUD is authored **anchor-relative to the visible picture rect**, never the window, with the 7.0 safe margin of 5 % of the picture rounded up to whole HUD px per axis (registry `safe_margin`, the HUD & Suit Layer's formula): 32 × 18 HUD px at 1920×1080, H 3; 22 × 14 HUD px at 1280×800, H 3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)* — and must survive a fractional HUD canvas (the picture divided by H is not always integer) and both aspects (C-R). The Deck has no notch; the margin is ergonomic and the ux-designer may raise it per device. Deck *text* size is PR-12's problem.
94	
95	*Fullscreen.* Default `MODE_FULLSCREEN` (borderless window covering the screen, `Window.mode = 3` `[BIN]`) rather than `EXCLUSIVE_FULLSCREEN` for Alt-Tab safety `[UNV]`; any mode or size change fires `Viewport.size_changed` `[BIN]` and is handled as one `RESCALING` frame (C.2) by **one pipeline-root node that is the only writer** of `SubViewport.size`, `size_2d_override` and the camera limits rect (consumed by the solver, C8), and the only caller of `HudLayout` (the HUD & Suit Layer's layout function, which computes the HUD anchors) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)* (→ ADR, with PR-7's wiring).
96	
97	---
98	
99	**PR-3. The layer model.** One root viewport, one world viewport, and `CanvasLayer`s above it. The question that assigns a thing to a layer is 7.0's: *who produced the information?* — the ship goes in the world and must be lit to read; the suit and the chart table are screen-space and never lit. **The HUD is in a different viewport, not merely a different layer** (engine-programmer): world lights, glow, `CanvasModulate`, the Filter pass on the container and the camera transform cannot reach it by construction, so HR-1, HR-6 and HR-13 are promised structurally. The trade-off is that nothing that must *mix* (a diegetic element lit by the world) may live there — it goes in the world.
100	
101	| # | Layer (bottom → top) | Where | Scaled by | Lit / glow / ambient / occlusion | Perception Filter | Camera jolt | Contents |
102	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
103	| 0 | **World** | `SubViewport` inside a `SubViewportContainer` | k | **yes** — the only layer that is (`use_hdr_2d`, `use_debanding`, filter, snap set on this viewport's own members `[BIN]`; never on the root, which stays SDR-exact for the 4.6 palette) | per-node effects inside; the full-screen pass sits on the container (PR-10) | yes (bounded, PR-6 C7) | floors, floor marks, the Y-sorted layer, caps, lights, occluders, fringe, dust, horrors, web, in-world instruments, the camera |
104	| 1 | **Transit / load hold** | `CanvasLayer` | — | no | no | no | one opaque black quad, shown only in `TRANSIT_HOLD` and `BOOTING/LOADING` (C.2) |
105	| 2 | **Suit layer (HUD)** | `CanvasLayer` | H | **no** (HR-1 by construction) | no — readings are fed *perceived values* by the Filter as data; the frame is fed nothing (7.6 hand-off) | **never** (HR-13); prompts use the unjolted transform (C11) | critical strip, suit panel, hand rail, crew strip, interaction prompts, inspect card |
106	| 3 | **Chart table / menus** | `CanvasLayer` | H (bitmap face), continuous (reading face) | no | no | no | pause panel over the frozen world (7.4), web map, settings, text chat |
107	| 4 | **Debug overlay** | `CanvasLayer`, dev builds only | H | no | **no — it reads the true channel** | no | DIAGNOSTIC surface (C.3); may toggle debug draws *inside* the world viewport (note e) |
108	
109	Rules that follow: (a) **glow is per viewport** (8.11 flag 3; 4.6 reworked glow to run before tonemapping `[REF]`, so no older tuning transfers and `glow_hdr_threshold` is re-found at 8.12 step 8). (b) The ambient-floor hull material (8.11 flag 1) and the HR-15 low-vision raise are **Lighting's**, applied inside layer 0; the pipeline owns no ambient value and **no full-frame gamma or brightness control exists anywhere** (C-R): the only brightness control the game has is HR-15's bounded hull-material step, which can never reveal web, horrors or filaments and never touches the HUD. (c) In-world instruments are layer-0 lit sprites; the inspect card (7.0) is layer 2 — the same reading drawn twice, once lit and once not. (d) Interaction prompts are layer 2 and are *gated* by the Emitter State exposure query, never by the renderer. 110	
111	*Alternative rejected:* HUD inside the world viewport with `LIGHT_MODE_UNSHADED` materials — unshaded items still receive glow and the full-screen Filter pass, so HR-1 would be a per-node discipline that one forgotten material breaks (8.11 flag 3 made this call; recorded here because the pipeline inherits it).
112	
113	---
114	
115	**PR-4. Pixel integrity.** Inside the world viewport:
116	
117	1. **Nearest sampling everywhere** (`light_` textures excepted — sampled by the light, not the item, 8.4). Mipmaps off on every drawn sheet (8.7).
118	2. **Integer base-px placement by presentation code — the viewport snap flags are a safety net, not the mechanism** (gameplay-programmer, engine-programmer). Because the world canvas *is* the body frame (PR-6 C2), no fractional body offset ever enters an interior position; other bodies drawn in this frame (a docked derelict, a detaching section) are placed by one floored offset shared by all their items, so their items never swim against each other.
119	3. **Interpolate, then quantise.** Rounding before interpolating produces 1 px stalls; interpolating after rounding is impossible. Consequence to state honestly (engine-programmer): **snap is a floor, not a filter** — interpolation changes only the *timing* of one-base-px steps, never their size. A body moving 1 base px per tick shows a k×k screen block step whenever it moves; the promise is "base-pixel steps at interpolated timing, never twice in a frame at f_render ≥ 60 (below that 1–2 base px per frame at 30–59 fps), never backward", not sub-pixel smoothness *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4)*. The Player Controller should therefore choose walk and run speeds in **whole base px per tick** when the camera quantum is 1 (PR-6 C3) — routed.
120	4. **Scale.** Only integer scales, only k (or the zoom step). Horizontal flips are permitted (mirrored facings, 5.6). No per-node scale animation of any kind; `Control.scale` stays `(1,1)` on the HUD. `Camera2D.zoom` stays `(1,1)` **always** (there is no pixel-snap member on `Camera2D` — confirmed by the exhaustive `[BIN]` member list — so zoom is a change of k, PR-6 C6).
121	5. **Rotation.** `Camera2D.rotation = 0` always, forever (game-designer; also `ignore_rotation = true` default `[BIN]`). Human-built geometry — floors, walls, caps, doors, props, machinery, pipes, seams, characters, tools, overlays, HUD — is **never rotated at runtime** (8.4): a lint asserts `rotation == 0` on every node under the environment, pipe, prop and actor groups. Rotation is permitted for **web pieces** (off-grid by design, 3.3), **horror rig segments** (quantised to 15°, stepped at 12 fps = every 5th tick, 5.4/8.10 — a test), and **lights** (engine light lives off the grid by 8.0's rule). Horror Entities' floor marks (smear, rime, radial hairlines, struck) are **not** web pieces: they are flip-only and never rotated (Horror C-HE-1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from horror-entities)*. What "rotated segments fall off the grid" means per pass: under pass A a rotated segment is rasterised at base resolution — a stair-step of whole base px, on the grid; under pass B it is rasterised at window resolution with nearest sampling — angled k×k blocks, same density, **off** the grid. The second is tolerated for horrors and web only (8.4); if it fails review the remedies are 8.10's (24-angle pre-rotated sets, or a base-resolution sub-viewport for horrors alone → ADR). `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel`'s effect on a rotated quad's corners is NOT SOURCEABLE — step 2 judges the rotating segment. Sub-pixel blur is forbidden in every case.
122	6. **Half-pixel origins.** `Sprite2D.centered = true` by default `[BIN]`: an odd-dimension texture centred puts its origin on a .5 and wobbles 1 px under NEAREST. 8.2's cells are even (48, 80, 96) and the foot origin (horizontally centred, the top row of the `foot_box`; registry `foot_box`) is set via `offset` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics)*, so the asset standard satisfies this; the rule for VFX and one-off sprites is **even cells, or `centered = false` with an integer `offset`**.
123	7. **No sub-pixel sprite positions** means no item is ever drawn at a fractional base-px offset *relative to the grid the other items are on*. Whether the whole grid may translate by screen pixels is the camera quantum's question (PR-6 C3), not this rule's.
124	8. **One interpolator.** The kernel's `tick_alpha` with previous/current read views is the only interpolator of sim-owned motion: `physics/common/physics_interpolation = false`, every presentation node `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF`, `Camera2D.position_smoothing_enabled = false`, `limit_smoothed = false` `[BIN]`. Decisive `[BIN]` reason beyond "two clocks": `get_global_transform_interpolated()` exists on `Node3D` only, so no 2D script could read where an engine-interpolated body is actually drawn — the camera would follow the un-interpolated pose and swim 1–3 render px against the sprite at 144 fps while looking fine at 60. The 2D interpolation machinery does exist in 4.7.2 `[BIN]` (items, lights, occluders); its behaviour is NOT SOURCEABLE and it is simply not used for sim-owned transforms. → ADR (interpolation clock). Whether pure-physics debris may use it is Ship Body's.
125	9. **Light masks.** `Light2D.range_item_cull_mask` and `CanvasItem.light_mask` default to bit 1 `[BIN]`; the unshaded emissive overlay and the fringe sprites go on a light-mask bit the beams do not light (6.2 "unshaded") — behaviour `[UNV]`, checked at 8.12 step 4. Bit 3 (decoys) and bits 4 and up (one per live body) are allocated by Lighting (LO-24) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from 2d-lighting-and-occlusion)*.
126	10. **Lines are sprites.** Hairlines, filaments and seams are sprites, never runtime line draws (8.4, `[REF]`).
127	
128	---
129	
130	**PR-5. Projection convention and the draw-order contract (3/4 oblique).** The projection is 1:1 with no foreshortening (8.2): one base px of floor depth, one of width and one of height are each one screen row or column. Floors are 48×48 squares (registry: `TILE_PX`). A wall has a **24 px footprint** on the floor grid, a **72 px front face** and a **24 px top cap**, occupying 96 screen rows but half a tile of floor.

3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

Constraints on what the pass may do (ux-designer, adopted; the Filter GDD owns the effects): it **writes colour only** — no displacement, blur, chromatic aberration, pixelation or resolution change; it **only adds** violet or flesh at 4.4's places and never remaps sane hues, erodes shape or trail contrast, or drops hull below the measured floor; it obeys the flash clamp (PR-13); it never writes a camera or viewport property (C1). Its output is **multiplied by a truth-channel mask** — character sprites, hand tools, crewmate beams, trails, the true cone edge — **or decomposed into per-element materials** so truth-channel pixels are exact (C-R). Everything stage 2/3 does to the *whole image* goes in this slot; everything *per thing* — a lying gauge's gleam, a decoy light, a wholly substituted sprite (5.0) — goes on nodes inside layer 0 under PR-8: the Filter's own per-node materials; modifier state that Lighting reads (LO-18); and decoy overlays — Filter-owned lies that Lighting draws as unshaded sprites on light-mask bit 3 (LO-21, LO-24) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from perception-filter and 2d-lighting-and-occlusion)*. **The mask's production is → ADR**: (a) a second `SubViewport` sharing the camera pose that draws only truth-channel items as unlit silhouettes (cheap, no sort problem because it is a mask, not a composite), or (b) no mask, per-element materials only; the Filter GDD chooses — and has chosen (b) for MVP (`filter_route = PER_ELEMENT`: the container slot is `NOT_USED`, its material null by design; route (a) is a VS-A option only if the lighting spike proves an exact mask) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from perception-filter)*. *Alternative rejected:* compositing truth-channel items in a second viewport **above** the filtered world — those items sort against corruptible ones on the same Y-sorted layer, and splitting a sorted layer across two viewports breaks PR-5. `BackBufferCopy` without the material slot is the engine alternative (8.10) → ADR.
214	
215	---
216	
217	**PR-11. Frame-rate independence.** The sim runs at 60 Hz (CR-1); the pipeline renders at whatever rate the display and settings allow and never changes the tick. **The acceptance test is the kernel's:** identical `state_hash` after a scripted 10-s input replay at `max_fps` 30, 60, 144 and 0 (G3 + CR-11; spike step 13).
218	
219	| Render rate | Ticks per frame | What presentation shows | Notes |
220	|---|---|---|---|
221	| 144 fps | 0 or 1 (ticks on ≈ 42 % of frames) | interpolated positions between the last two commits at `tick_alpha ∈ [0,1)`, floored: camera and sprites step one base px at the interpolated instant, **never twice in a frame (this holds for every f_render ≥ 60 Hz = the tick rate; below 60 a frame spans more than one tick and a 1 px/tick body steps 1 or 2 base px — the 40 and 30 fps rows) and never backward** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4)*; without interpolation 58 % of frames would repeat a pose | no sub-base-pixel motion exists at any fps unless the `1/k` quantum is adopted (C3); `L_render` shrinks to ≤ 6.9 ms, input latency is otherwise unchanged above 60 |
222	| 60 fps | 1 | with tick-before-render, `tick_alpha` at draw time is ≈ 0, so an **interpolated transform shows approximately the *previous* tick's position**: continuous motion carries **one tick (≈ 17 ms) of visual latency by construction**, because D.3 forbids extrapolation. **Discrete committed state** (a light toggled, a gauge value, a trail appearing) reads `current` and shows in the same frame — D.4's best case applies to it. Look-ahead reads the **raw** aim (C4) and so carries no tick | the design target; the latency is the price of the honest clamp and is the same at every fps |
223	| 30 fps | 2 (catch-up) | the latest commit; `tick_alpha` clamps at 1 after the second tick; motion shows every second tick's pose — 2-base-px steps for a 1 px/tick body, honest, not smoothed | input-to-pixel worst case 50 ms (D.4); acceptable; **the Deck floor under pass A** |
224	| 40 / 90 Hz (Deck panels) | 1.5 / 0.67 average | the interpolation path is what keeps motion even at rates that are not multiples of 60. At 90 Hz (0.67 ticks per frame) the step is 0 or +1 base px, the same promise as 144 fps. At 40 Hz (1.5 ticks per frame, ticks per frame alternating 2, 1) a 1 px/tick body steps +1, +2, +1, +2 base px per frame: whole base pixels, never fractional, never backward, honest and unsmoothed like the 30 fps row; the "never twice in a frame" promise does not apply below 60 fps *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4)* | spike at 40 and 90 fps caps (step 13) |
225	| < 20 fps | up to `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`, then sim-time lag (CR-17) | the latest commit; the world *slows* rather than extrapolates; a catch-up burst is ≤ 12 px and eases; only a named ≥ 48 px source (weld delta, Body shove, restore) triggers the camera cut (C5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | the pipeline reports frame time to the Debug Overlay; never a visual compensation |

227	`tick_alpha` is clamped at 1 so a hitch holds the last pose rather than extrapolating (D.3's Pillar 1 argument). Presentation reads `delta` only to advance `present_time` and the solver's smoothing. **Tick driver (settled in ADR-0001, Proposed; kernel CR-1a):** the kernel's `TickDriver` runs from the `_process` of one always-processing host node, so the physics step is not the clock and there is one accumulator (kernel D.5). `physics_jitter_fix`, `max_physics_steps_per_frame` and `physics_ticks_per_second` stay at engine defaults; spike KRN-LAT-02 records their measured effect on the tick pattern rather than assuming none. `delta_smoothing` `[BIN]` acts on the `_process` delta the driver converts to `delta_us` `[UNV]`, and the spike records it. **Order inside a frame** is fixed by process priority (Adapter, then driver, then presentation; ADR-0001 § 2), which the spike verifies on a dev build and a release export. **Position ownership (settled):** Ship Body owns ship-local kinematic position and integrates it inside the tick (kernel CR-4), so kernel `tick_alpha` is the one interpolator. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — ADR-0001 GDD sync)* **V-sync and caps (PR-14):** ship `VSYNC_ENABLED` (engine default `[BIN]`); expose `MAILBOX` as "uncapped, no tearing" and `DISABLED` + `max_fps` for benchmarking; never `ADAPTIVE` by default (behaviour on Windows D3D12 vs Vulkan NOT SOURCEABLE — the binary reports `driver.windows = vulkan` `[BIN]` while `[REF]` says D3D12 is the 4.6+ default; 8.12 step 1 prints the active driver and the GDD assumes neither).

231	**PR-12. HUD scale.** The HUD's integer scale is `H ∈ {H_default, …, 2·H_default}` with **`H_default = max(k, 3)`** — **never below 3× on any display** (registry: `HUD_MIN_SCALE` = 3) (C-R), player-raisable to 2× the default in integer steps (HR-12's 100–200 %), labelled in Settings **by resulting cap height in screen px** (e.g. "21 px / 28 px / 35 px / 42 px" at 1080p), not by percentage (ux-designer). At 1080p the steps are 3×–6×; on the Deck and at 720p **3×–6× over a 2× world**; the Settings screen offers only the steps where the HUD's `bottom_row_fit` holds (registry; `H_default` always — the fallback when `fit` is false; H 5 and 6 are not offered at a 1280-px picture until CF-HS-11 is resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*; at 1440p 4×–8×; at 2160p 6×–12×. H is **independent of k and of zoom** (8.1: "the frame grows, the world does not"). The reading face (7.1) scales continuously and is the only non-integer text in the game. **Reading-face rasterisation** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: reading-face text is rasterised by the font server at its **final screen pixel size** (the label's font size is set to `round(base_size · scale_pct · window_scale)` on a `Control` chain whose `CanvasLayer.scale` and `Control.scale` are `(1, 1)` and whose own size is in screen px), and is never drawn under an integer-scaled `CanvasLayer` (`scale = H`) or under the world container's scale, where the same glyphs would be bitmap-stretched and blur; the pixel-grid faces (HUD) keep the integer `H` path. How layers 3–4, which sit at root scale, receive screen-px sizes under each wiring is part of the wiring ADR `[UNV]`; the acceptance test is a screenshot at 100 %, 125 % and 200 % showing crisp glyph edges (manual). Consequences: (i) because the Deck ships at H = 3 over k = 2, **two integer scales in one window is an MVP requirement**, not a post-spike nicety — it is PR-7's wiring ADR; the engine-programmer's note that "the HUD's integer scale comes from the root stretch with `Control.scale = (1,1)`" holds only when H = k, and `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels = true` `[BIN]` stays on the root in every wiring; (ii) **7.0's critical-strip size cap (12 % × 5 % of frame) is exceeded by default on the Deck** at H = 3 over a 2× world (the plate is 1.5× larger relative to the picture than at 1080p) — routed to art-director as a known, accepted cost of C-R's 3× floor — **resolved by the HUD & Suit Layer GDD**: the cap is defined at the 1080p reference frame and the Deck overage is accepted; a letterbox hairline, if used, is a layer-1 element excluded from the HUD count *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)*; (iii) the arcminute floors per device class (desk monitor, TV, handheld) that justify the 3× floor are the accessibility-specialist's table — routed. HUD elements are anchor-relative to the picture (PR-2) and survive a fractional HUD canvas. **The mechanism** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: "anchors absorb the fraction" is not one, because a `Control`'s anchors resolve against the root viewport, not the picture; instead the pipeline root sizes a **HUD-root `Control` to `hud_rect / H`** (a possibly fractional size, at the HUD rect's origin, the HUD rect being pinned to the `k_base` picture, PR-2) on every `RESCALING`, and every HUD element anchors to that Control; `world_to_hud` (D.14) returns coordinates relative to it. `H_default = max(k_auto, 3)` (unchanged).

233	---
234	
235	**PR-13. Photosensitivity and brightness.** The pipeline hosts the frame-level invariants; Lighting owns the per-light clamp through its modifier contract. (a) **Per light:** no light may produce more than **3 flashes per rolling 1-s window**, a flash being a pair of opposing luminance changes ≥ 10 %, red included (C-R); the alarm beacon's 2–3 s sweep (2.8) and the cryo lamp's gutter (0.3–0.5 s dips no more often than every 10–20 s, 2.2) pass; **the deployable's flicker (3.2) must be specified as a number and pass the clamp** — routed to art-director and technical-artist; the pipeline-side ceiling the art-director authors inside is at most 4 transitions per second (`F = 2`, one pair under `F_MAX`) at any amplitude ≥ 10 % (Open Question 6). **The clamp is analytic, not measured** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: Lighting computes each light's requested luminance transitions per tick from its modifier state (beacon sweep, cryo gutter, a deployable's flicker, a toggle), applies D.15's transition rule to that sequence and delays transitions *before* they are drawn; the regional and frame-mean sums use each light's luminance times its footprint in the region as an upper bound. A GPU readback is never in the clamp's path — it would either stall the frame or arrive frames late. (b) **Regional and frame-mean:** the same ceiling applies to each region of a 3 × 3 grid over the displayed picture at the current field (a ninth of it; 213 × 120 base px only at the default 640×360 field, 128 × 72 at the 384×216 field of `k_z` = 5 at 1080p — registry `flash_governor`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from 2d-lighting-and-occlusion)* and to the frame mean, so overlapping lights cannot sum past it; **no full-frame flash in any state, on any layer** (7.3, HR-13). (c) **A "reduce flashing" toggle, separate from reduced motion**: deployables steady, power arcs held as glow, the beacon becomes a static mark + sound + HUD glyph (HR-8's form), the cryo gutter kept. **The toggle defaults ON on a fresh profile, at first launch** (default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): creative-director recommendation, design-review decision D79 / X10; a player who wants the full effects turns it off in settings); reduced motion keeps its default OFF. While it is on, the strict ceiling of (g) applies to every source with no exemptions *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (d) **No full-frame gamma or brightness**; HR-15's bounded hull-material step is the only brightness control (PR-3 b). (e) A **first-launch photosensitivity notice** (chart-table register); it states that reduce flashing is already on and where to change it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (f) A **flash scan** of the 2.8 breach composition and the 2.4 lost state is a spike step (routed to the technical-artist's 8.12 list); the scan — a 3 × 3 region and frame-mean luminance reduction of the displayed picture, read back asynchronously so it is at least two frames late — is **verification only**, in dev builds and the flash-scan tool, absent from release builds, and costs at most 0.5 ms of GPU time on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (pending spike measurement; Open Question 20, closed by R12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*. (g) **Counting unit and area weighting** (user ruling 2026-10-27, design-review decision D91 / X9): the counting unit is `F = ceil(n_transitions / 2)` (D.15; registry `flash_count`), and the ceiling `F_MAX` = `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` = 3 is **weighted per area**: a region or the frame mean counts a transition only when the *area-weighted* change of its mean luminance reaches 10 % (D.15), so a change confined to a small patch does not count at region level. Two source classes are **exempt from the element-level count** (they still enter every region and frame-mean sum at their area weight): *sub-threshold digit swaps* (a HUD numeral change whose area-weighted change is under the 10 % rule) and *prompt show-starts* (a single step, spaced by the HUD's own floor of `ceil(TICK_RATE / F_MAX)` = 20 ticks). **Strict, never exempt:** the Alarm Red mark (counted per element with no area weighting) and **every source while reduce flashing is on** (exemptions suspended). The no-full-frame-flash rule of (b) is unchanged. The HUD owns its digit grid (`HONEST_TICK_MS` 500, ratified by the same ruling) and its mark behaviour; this section owns the unit and the rule *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The Filter pass obeys (a)–(b) (PR-10).

239	**PR-14. What Settings may expose (all integer; no non-integer option anywhere).** Display mode (windowed / fullscreen / borderless); resolution; **integer world scale** (Auto + list; a manual k below Auto forces `keep`, PR-2); HUD scale (labelled by cap height, PR-12); reading-face scale (continuous — the one exception, and it is text, not pixels); aspect `keep` / `expand` (post-spike); frame cap (30 / 60 / 120 / 144 / 240 / off); V-sync (enabled / mailbox / off); reduced motion (disables look-ahead, jolt → 0, world effects per HR-8 — never trail propagation, never `present_time`); reduce flashing (PR-13; **default ON at first launch**, default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the HR-15 ambient-floor step (Lighting's, surfaced here). Never: a camera smoothing slider that could introduce overshoot, a zoom level, a FOV, gamma, brightness, sharpening, or any filter.

241	---
242	
243	**PR-15. Guard rails (engine-programmer, adopted).** (1) The `[display]` stretch block (`mode = canvas_items`, `aspect = keep` for the spike, `scale_mode = integer`, 640×360), `default_texture_filter = 0`, both `snap_2d_*` keys, `hdr_2d` and `use_debanding` are **set to their required values in `project.godot`** (approval path 8.11 flag 7 — not Section C's to write; a value equal to the engine default is not serialised by the editor, so the tests read the *effective* value, not the key's presence) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **`use_debanding` and the "palette exact" promise** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the engine's debanding is a dither of about one least-significant bit added to the 8-bit output, which would perturb a flat palette fill and contradicts the SDR-exact palette promise of layer 0 (PR-3). The required value is therefore **`use_debanding = false` on the world viewport** (so also its engine default) **unless a spike item (step 1) shows both: (a) a flat fill of every palette entry reads back bit-exact with debanding on, and (b) a dark gradient that matters (the 0–1 % ambient) bands visibly with it off**; it may be switched on only if (a) and (b) both hold, and stays off otherwise (an AC reads back the flat fills, Startup assertions). The same item also carries: together with *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color = Color(0, 0, 0, 1)` — the "true black" letterbox bars are the engine clear colour, which defaults to a dark grey, so without this key PR-2's bars are not black; `display/window/size/window_width_override = 1280` and `window_height_override = 720` — otherwise an editor-launched game opens at the 640×360 viewport size, below `MIN_WINDOW`; the 4.7 **HDR-output flag explicitly off** (the ProjectSettings key name is NOT SOURCEABLE here — the 4.7 reference lists the feature but not the key — and is read from the 4.7.2 class dump at spike step 1; the 4.6 palette is SDR-exact, PR-3 layer 0); and `transparent_bg = false` stated explicitly on the world `SubViewport` and per-pixel window transparency not allowed on the root (so no layer ever composites against an alpha background). If wiring (i) wins (PR-7) the stretch keys read `mode = disabled`. (2) A **debug-build startup assertion** in the pipeline root reads back `content_scale_mode == CANVAS_ITEMS`, `content_scale_stretch == INTEGER`, `content_scale_size == (640, 360)`, the world `SubViewport`'s filter / snap / hdr / debanding members, the container filter (`== CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST`, the right enum per target), `physics_interpolation == false`, `position_smoothing_enabled == false`, `Camera2D.zoom == (1,1)`, the clear colour `== (0,0,0,1)`, the window size override `== (1280, 720)`, the HDR-output flag `== false`, the world `SubViewport` `transparent_bg == false`, and prints the driver name — failing loudly on any mismatch *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; (3) a **headless gdUnit4 test parses `project.godot`** for the same keys so the check runs in CI without a window; (4) a **debug-only tree walk** (every frame behind a console toggle) over the world viewport flags any `CanvasItem` whose position has a fractional part after presentation has written it, any `rotation != 0` under human-built groups, any `Camera2D.zoom != (1,1)`, any `Control.scale != (1,1)` on the HUD, Y-sort enabled on the floor layer, and a `TileSet.tile_size` of 16; (5) a scene-tree lint: no `Camera2D` descends from a `PhysicsBody2D`. The three failure modes these guard against — shipping the engine defaults, two clocks moving one thing, fractional transforms leaking into the world canvas — are the ones a solo first-time Godot developer most plausibly builds.

247	**Unresolved conflicts carried to Open Questions (not decided here).**
248	1. **Zoom on 2× displays.** C-R "no zoom-out below a 2× world" removes the zoom step on the Steam Deck, at 720p and under a manual 2× — but the game-designer made the player's zoom step one of the four mitigations for "across the room" readability and wants it "available in every state", and 5.6's 50 % gate is what makes a 1× world unreadable. Options for the user: accept no zoom on 2× displays (Deck players rely on look-ahead and kits alone); permit the 1× step on the Deck only, as a deliberate press (the 50 % marks test is still met — 5.6 tier 2 is defined at 50 %); or raise the Deck's base presentation (not possible without breaking 8.1). Routed to game-designer, ux-designer and creative-director. *(Superseded by the user-ruling note below — the ladder reaches 1× on every display; consistency check 2026-10-26.)*
249	2. **Exponential follow vs avatar jitter.** Decided in favour of `τ_follow = 0.18 s` (gameplay-programmer); the systems-designer's ±1 px avatar wobble concern is an A/B at step 12, not a reopening.
250	3. **C-R21 first-boot black-level calibration** reframes a user decision (no brightness control) — recorded as an Open Question for the user and creative-director, not adopted (Resolved 2026-10-26 — user decision, guide-only calibration; Open Question 5) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21: stale open wording closed)*.

content.content:
160	**C2. Frame: the world canvas is the current body's frame, interior at origin.** The interior scene of the body the avatar is on sits at the origin of the world viewport's canvas; **ship motion through the void never appears in the interior view** — it appears only on exterior or transit layers (`Parallax2D`/`ParallaxBackground` exist `[BIN]`), and **ship rotation is never rendered inside** (gameplay-programmer, engine-programmer option (a); routed to the Ship Body GDD). Consequences: (i) the render rotation of every human-built body is 0 and two docked bodies are both axis-aligned — a hard constraint exported to Ship Body (→ ADR there: `lock_rotation`, or rotate in simulation while presenting in the body frame); (ii) **detached sections translate without rotation in the interior view** (routed to Modular Ship Assembly); (iii) all pixel snapping is in the body frame (C-R), which PR-4 rule 2 already requires; (iv) the pod in transit is its own body — the camera is pod-local and the pod moves at constant velocity against the exterior layer (gameplay-programmer). The follow target is the local seat's controlled entity (kernel binding table, CR-7); **no shared camera in co-op** — every client has its own window. **The camera is a top-level presentation node, never a child of the body** (engine-programmer): `Camera2D.process_callback` is IDLE by default `[BIN]`, a parented camera would inherit the body's transform on the engine's clock and (without `ignore_rotation`) its rotation, and no 2D API exposes an interpolated global transform; the camera script composes the avatar's interpolated body-local position exactly as the actor's presentation node does, with `Node.process_priority` ordering it after the actor (behaviour `[UNV]`, step 12). If the two compose differently the camera lags the sprite by up to a tick — step 12's zero-render-px-disagreement test. **`Camera2D` applies its scroll in its own internal processing** (`process_callback` IDLE `[BIN]`), so the frame can show last frame's pose against this frame's sprites, and `process_priority` cannot fix that because the engine, not the script, applies the scroll `[UNV]`. The camera host therefore **writes the world viewport's `canvas_transform` directly** from `pose_q` (plus the jolt offset) in a **named hook: the pipeline root's `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` handler `[UNV]` (the signal that fires after the scene tree's `_process` and before the frame is drawn; its existence and ordering against `Node.process_priority` are verified at spike step 12; the fallback hook is the pipeline root's own `_process` at the lowest `process_priority`, which still precedes the draw)**, after every presentation node has written its position *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier "render callback" named no hook)*, so there is no engine scroll to lag; the accepted alternative, if the ADR rejects the direct write, is a `Camera2D` with `anchor_mode = ANCHOR_MODE_FIXED_TOP_LEFT`, drag margins off and `force_update_scroll()` called after each write. Either way **the solver is the only clamp**: `Camera2D.limit_*` stays at the engine defaults (unused), so limits are never clamped twice and `world_to_hud` is never offset while `CLAMPED` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Two variants, every camera assertion dual-pathed; parallax** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the **primary variant** writes `canvas_transform` directly and has **no `Camera2D` in the world tree**; the **alternative** is the `Camera2D` of the previous sentence. Every assertion and lint in this GDD that names a `Camera2D` property (`zoom == (1,1)`, `position_smoothing_enabled == false`, `limit_smoothed == false`, `limit_*` at defaults, `process_callback`, the no-physics-parent lint) is read as "holds on the `Camera2D` **if the variant has one**", and each has a primary-variant twin: the world viewport's `canvas_transform` has scale `(1, 1)` and no rotation or skew on every frame, its origin is written by the camera host only, the world tree contains zero `Camera2D` nodes (a lint), and nothing but the host writes `canvas_transform`. **Parallax:** `Parallax2D` / `ParallaxBackground` is assumed to need a `Camera2D` to read the scroll `[UNV]`, so in the primary variant the exterior and transit layers would freeze; and a `scroll_scale` other than 1 gives fractional offsets, which break the grid. The rule is therefore that **the camera host drives every exterior and transit layer itself**: `layer.position = −floor(pose_q · scroll_scale)` rounded to whole base px (so a non-1 `scroll_scale` never gives a fractional offset), written in the same hook as the canvas transform; `Parallax2D` is used only if the spike proves it follows a direct `canvas_transform` write **and** yields whole-base-px offsets, in which case the host drives nothing.
161	
162	**C3. The solver: a pure function, first-order smoothing, quantised after.** The camera is a `CameraSolver` — a pure `RefCounted` `solve(input, state, params) → pose` with no scene-tree dependency, headless-testable, deterministic, and **frame-rate independent within a stated bound** (gameplay-programmer; → ADR for the node that hosts it): the per-frame factor is exact for a target held constant through the frame, but for a moving target the lag measured after the update, `|target_n − f_n|`, is `v·τ·h/(e^h − 1)` with `h = dt/τ` — 30.9 px at 60 fps, 31.8 px at 144 fps and 29.5 px at 30 fps against the dt→0 limit `v·τ` = 32.4 px at `v_max` (D.6) — so the contract is *the same quantised pose to within 1 base px on a continuous target trace*, never bit-identity, and `v·τ` is the conservative bound every invariant uses (the lag after the update is strictly smaller at every `dt > 0`, so low render rates do not erode the inner-box margin) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Its follow is a **first-order exponential approach** `cam += (target − cam) × (1 − exp(−dt / τ_follow))` with `τ_follow ≈ 0.18 s` — zero overshoot by construction, so the camera **never reverses direction within 100 ms unless the player did** (C-R). **Settle:** an exponential never arrives, and `floor()` of an asymptotic approach lands one pixel late or never, so every pose term snaps to its target per axis once it is within `SETTLE_EPS = 0.5·Q` (0.5 base px at `Q = 1`): `f → target`, `L → L_target` (D.6, D.7). The solver keeps its state as float64 scalars per axis (never `Vector2`, which is float32 and can stall one ulp short of a target), and the settle makes any residual stall irrelevant. A still scene's pose is therefore constant after a bounded settle and equals `floor(target + L_target)`, including with `L_MAX = 0` (reduced motion); the last pixel of a settle can land up to `t_settle = τ_eff·ln(|d₀| / SETTLE_EPS)` after the avatar stops (≈ 0.75 s from a 32.4 px lag) and is the final step of a motion the avatar caused *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **No dead-zone** (knob `DEAD_ZONE`, default 0 × 0, kept for A/B). The crewmate is confined to an **inner box ≈ 0.60 of the frame** (half-extents 0.30 × frame = ±192 × ±108 base px about centre at 640×360): follow lag plus look-ahead may never push the avatar outside it. The pose is **quantised after smoothing** to the camera quantum `QUANTUM ∈ {1 base px, 1/k base px}`; **MVP ships on 1** (whole base px in the body frame — C-R), and the `1/k` path — render the world viewport 2 base px larger with the camera at `floor(cam) − (1,1)` and offset the `SubViewportContainer` by `−round((1 + frac(cam)) × k)` screen px, so the picture scrolls in screen-pixel steps while every item stays on one shared base grid — is **built as the upgrade if testers name the stutter** (gameplay-programmer). The `1/k` path costs 2 px overdraw, a container clipped to the picture rect (bars stay untouched), root snap off for the container's fractional root position (shares PR-7's wiring ADR), its pass-B behaviour is `[UNV]`, and it needs **art-director sign-off against 8.0** (the grid translates; its contents do not) **and ux-designer sign-off against C-R "camera moves in whole base px in its body frame"**, which the `1/k` path relaxes to whole screen px. *Systems-designer's recorded risk, for step 12:* with exponential follow and camera and avatar floored independently, the avatar's screen position wobbles ±1 px whenever their fractional parts cross — the one artefact 8.0's grid makes most visible, on the one sprite always on screen. A rigid follow (camera = avatar + offset, smoothing only on the offset) avoids it at the cost of the world scrolling in the avatar's cadence; the A/B is `τ_follow` = 0.18 vs 0 with `DEAD_ZONE` = 0, measured in step 12 as camera-vs-sprite jitter in render px. **Threshold and fallback (step 12):** during a constant-speed walk at `v_walk` and at `v_run`, count the changes of the avatar-to-screen offset `p − pose_q` (base px) from `t_exact` = 10·`τ_eff` = 1.8 s after the run starts from rest (D.6; `3·τ_eff` is only the 95 % time) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the exponential follow ships only if the count is ≤ 2 per second at 60, 90 and 144 fps (PROVISIONAL — the ux-designer ratifies against the footage), and a miss ships **D.6b, the offset-quantised follow** (`pose_q = p + floor(clamp(f − target + L))`: the lag is kept as a constant offset and the camera steps with the sprite, the world scrolling in the avatar's cadence; pure rigid follow is D.6b at `τ_follow` = 0) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: D.6b is now specified and is the default candidate; the camera-solver story is not ready until D.6b's ACs exist and run)*. The arithmetic predicts a miss above the tick rate: the steady lag `v·τ` is not an integer, so `⌊T⌋ − ⌊T − lag⌋` alternates between two values twice per base px of travel once the render rate exceeds 60 fps (at an integer-speed 60 fps both terms land on integers and the offset is constant) — rigid follow is therefore a likely outcome at 144 fps, not a remote one *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
